summary.big_en: We share feelings with the people around us, and the present perfect is how we talk about what has just happened.

grammar.title: Present perfect
grammar.when: Use the present perfect for events in the recent past, when the time of the event is not important.
grammar.form: have / has + past participle

examples.en: I have drawn a car.
examples.why: the drawing is finished; when is not the point

examples.en: Have you finished yet?
examples.why: question form: have + subject + past participle

examples.en: I have never been afraid of water again.
examples.why: an experience that covers up to now

examples.en: But I haven't been on a rollercoaster again!
examples.why: negative: have + not + past participle

grammar.watch: Ask 'Have you ever…?' when you want to know about someone's experience (p.19).

words.title: Identity and feelings

items.def: The things that make you who you are.
items.example: Your name and your language are both part of your identity.
items.example_vi: Tên và tiếng nói của em đều là một phần bản sắc của em.

items.def: To come first in a game or competition.
items.example: Our team won the match by two goals.
items.example_vi: Đội của chúng tôi thắng trận với cách biệt hai bàn.

items.def: To hurt or frighten someone weaker, again and again.
items.example: Nobody should bully a younger child at school.
items.example_vi: Không ai được bắt nạt em nhỏ hơn ở trường.

items.def: Very good indeed.
items.example: The view from the top of the mountain was awesome.
items.example_vi: Khung cảnh từ đỉnh núi đẹp đến kinh ngạc.

items.def: Unkind to other people.
items.example: It was mean of him to laugh at her drawing.
items.example_vi: Cậu ấy cười nhạo bức vẽ của bạn là rất ác ý.

items.def: Damage or injury done to someone or something.
items.example: Too much sun can harm your skin.
items.example_vi: Nắng nhiều quá có thể làm hại da của bạn.

items.def: To suffer or die because there is no food.
items.example: Without rain the crops fail and people starve.
items.example_vi: Không có mưa thì mùa màng mất trắng và người ta chết đói.

summary.big_en: Latitude and longitude let you pinpoint any place on Earth, and prepositions link the nouns that describe it.

grammar.title: Prepositions before nouns
grammar.when: A preposition shows the connection between nouns and adjectives in a sentence.
grammar.form: preposition + noun

examples.en: … places on our planet
examples.why: on + noun

examples.en: … parallel to the equator
examples.why: adjective + to + noun

examples.en: Lines of longitude run from the North Pole to the South Pole.
examples.why: from … to … with nouns

examples.en: … one of the hottest places on our planet
examples.why: the model sentence in Activity 7

words.title: Map reading

items.def: The most northern or the most southern point of the Earth.
items.example: At one end is the North Pole and at the other, the South Pole.
items.example_vi: Một đầu là Bắc Cực, đầu kia là Nam Cực.

items.def: A unit of measurement.
items.example: The equator's line of latitude is zero degrees.
items.example_vi: Đường vĩ tuyến của xích đạo là không độ.

items.def: Two lines that stay the same distance apart.
items.example: More lines of latitude circle the Earth parallel to the equator.
items.example_vi: Các vĩ tuyến khác vòng quanh Trái Đất song song với xích đạo.

items.def: Standing upwards.
items.example: The lines divide the Earth's surface into vertical sections.
items.example_vi: Các đường này chia bề mặt Trái Đất thành những phần thẳng đứng.

items.def: A code that shows an exact position on a map.
items.example: Bangkok is at the coordinate 13° N 100° E.
items.example_vi: Bangkok nằm ở toạ độ 13° Bắc 100° Đông.

items.def: Lines that circle the Earth parallel to the equator.
items.example: Lines of latitude are measured 0–90° to the north and to the south.
items.example_vi: Vĩ tuyến được đo từ 0 đến 90 độ về phía bắc và phía nam.

items.def: Lines that run from the North Pole to the South Pole.
items.example: Lines of longitude divide the Earth's surface into vertical sections.
items.example_vi: Kinh tuyến chia bề mặt Trái Đất thành những phần thẳng đứng.

items.def: The imaginary line circling the Earth halfway between the poles.
items.example: In the middle, circling the Earth between the two poles, is the equator.
items.example_vi: Ở giữa, vòng quanh Trái Đất giữa hai cực, là đường xích đạo.

words.note: pole, degree, parallel, vertical and coordinate are the book's Key words box (p.15); the other three come from the text itself.

readings.title: Geography: how we map the Earth
readings.about: Lines of latitude circle the Earth parallel to the equator and lines of longitude run pole to pole, so any place can be given as a coordinate.

summary.big_en: A good presentation about someone you admire needs an opening that grabs attention and words that show the order of your ideas.

items.def: A person who takes action to support their beliefs.
items.example: Malala Yousafzai is an activist for girls' education.
items.example_vi: Malala Yousafzai là nhà hoạt động vì quyền học tập của trẻ em gái.

items.def: To think very well of someone.
items.example: I admire her because she never gave up.
items.example_vi: Em khâm phục cô ấy vì cô ấy không bao giờ bỏ cuộc.

items.def: To refuse to allow something.
items.example: They banned girls from going to school.
items.example_vi: Họ cấm các bé gái đến trường.

items.def: The internet, newspapers, TV and magazines.
items.example: Her story appeared in the media all over the world.
items.example_vi: Câu chuyện của cô ấy xuất hiện trên truyền thông khắp thế giới.

items.def: To disagree and complain very strongly.
items.example: People protested when the school was closed.
items.example_vi: Mọi người phản đối khi ngôi trường bị đóng cửa.

items.def: To organise activities to achieve something.
items.example: She campaigns for girls' education.
items.example_vi: Cô ấy vận động cho quyền học tập của trẻ em gái.

items.def: The first part of a talk, where you say what it is about.
items.example: As I said in my introduction, she is a young activist.
items.example_vi: Như em đã nói ở phần mở đầu, cô ấy là một nhà hoạt động trẻ.

items.def: Words and phrases that show your audience the order of your ideas.
items.example: Sequencing words like 'to sum up' help your audience follow you.
items.example_vi: Những từ nối như 'tóm lại' giúp người nghe theo được mạch bài.

sounds.title: -tion and -sion endings
sounds.focus: Both endings are one unstressed syllable, /ən/, and the letter before it is not said as it is spelled. -tion is 'shun' /ʃən/, but -sion after a vowel is 'zhun' /ʒən/.
sounds.note: The stress always lands on the syllable just before the ending: intro-DUC-tion, edu-CA-tion, de-CI-sion, presen-TA-tion.

lines: Today, I'm going to talk about…
As I said in my introduction, she is a…
By this time, she was…
Since then, with her father, she…
To sum up, I chose to…

readings.about: Aliya explains why she chose Malala, tells her early life and her work, and ends by saying why she admires her.

summary.big_en: Describing a first-time experience means naming what you did and the feelings it gave you.

grammar.title: verb + direct object + infinitive
grammar.when: Some verbs take a person first and then an infinitive with 'to'.
grammar.form: verb + object + to + verb

examples.en: My friend asked me to go with him.
examples.why: asked + me + to go

examples.en: My dad taught me to swim.
examples.why: taught + me + to swim

grammar.watch: Activity 5 asks you to find another example of this pattern in Cody's description (p.19).

words.title: Adjectives and their noun forms

items.def: So surprising that you can hardly believe it.
items.example: I looked at it in amazement.
items.example_vi: Em nhìn nó mà kinh ngạc.

items.def: Making you feel happy and full of energy.
items.example: I remember that feeling of excitement very well.
items.example_vi: Em nhớ rất rõ cảm giác phấn khích đó.

items.def: Making you feel very frightened.
items.example: It was exciting and terrifying at the same time.
items.example_vi: Nó vừa phấn khích vừa đáng sợ cùng một lúc.

items.def: Pleased about something good you have done.
items.example: I felt a sense of pride for doing something brave.
items.example_vi: Em thấy tự hào vì đã làm được một việc dũng cảm.

items.def: Pleased because you got what you wanted.
items.example: I felt very satisfied because I had achieved something big.
items.example_vi: Em thấy rất mãn nguyện vì đã làm được một việc lớn.

words.note: Most of these add -ment or -tion to the adjective. Two do not: proud → pride and terrifying → terror, so learn those two as pairs.

readings.title: First-time experiences
readings.about: Santok rode a rollercoaster, Olivia saw the sea, and Cody learned to swim; each says what happened and how it felt.

summary.big_en: A story can tell you more than it says: you read the clues and work the rest out yourself.

items.def: Shaped like a bird's beak.
items.example: My nose would be on the beaky side.
items.example_vi: Mũi em thì hơi khoằm như mỏ chim.

items.def: To move quickly with a short, light movement.
items.example: I have white-blond hair that flicks around my face.
items.example_vi: Em có mái tóc vàng bạch kim hất tung quanh mặt.

items.def: Not like most others; not common.
items.example: A girl with an unusual name tells her own story.
items.example_vi: Một cô bé có cái tên khác thường tự kể chuyện mình.

readings.title: A Girl Called Owl, by Amy Wilson
readings.about: A girl called Owl explains how she got her unusual name and how her own features seem to match it.

summary.big_en: Sport is part of everyday life, and every sport needs its own words and its own equipment.

words.title: Sports equipment

items.def: The small light object that you hit over the net in badminton.
items.example: You need a shuttlecock to play badminton.
items.example_vi: Bạn cần một quả cầu để chơi cầu lông.

items.def: A bat with strings, used in tennis and badminton.
items.example: She holds the racquet in her right hand when she serves.
items.example_vi: Bạn ấy cầm vợt bằng tay phải khi giao bóng.

items.def: Special glasses that protect your eyes, for example when you swim.
items.example: Swimmers wear goggles so that the water does not hurt their eyes.
items.example_vi: Người bơi đeo kính bơi để nước không làm cay mắt.

items.def: Hard pads that protect the front of your lower legs.
items.example: Footballers wear shin pads to protect the front of their legs.
items.example_vi: Cầu thủ bóng đá đeo bọc ống chân để bảo vệ phần trước cẳng chân.

items.def: The two posts that stand at each end of a football or hockey pitch.
items.example: The ball hit the goalposts and bounced back onto the pitch.
items.example_vi: Quả bóng đập vào cột gôn rồi bật ngược lại sân.

items.def: Material with holes in it, stretched across a court or across a goal.
items.example: In tennis and volleyball you have to hit the ball over the net.
items.example_vi: Trong quần vợt và bóng chuyền, bạn phải đánh bóng qua lưới.

items.def: A long stick with a curved end, used to hit the ball in hockey.
items.example: You need a hockey stick and a small hard ball to play hockey.
items.example_vi: Bạn cần một cây gậy và một quả bóng nhỏ cứng để chơi khúc côn cầu.

items.def: A band you wear around your waist; in judo its colour shows your level.
items.example: In judo, the colour of your belt shows how much you have learned.
items.example_vi: Trong judo, màu đai cho biết bạn đã học được tới đâu.

words.note: Activity 7 asks you to say what each sport needs: 'You need a shuttlecock to play badminton.'

readings.title: Four children talk about their sports
readings.about: Four children say which sport they do and give their reasons for liking it. Activity 5 asks you to compare their reasons with your own.

summary.big_en: What you eat changes how much energy your body has for sport, and the 1st conditional is how you talk about those likely results.

grammar.title: 1st conditional with if / unless
grammar.when: Use the 1st conditional for future events that are likely to happen.
grammar.form: if / unless + present simple, + will / won't + verb

examples.en: If you drink plenty of water, you'll stay hydrated.
examples.why: if + present simple, then will + verb

examples.en: Your body won't grow well unless you get plenty of protein.
examples.why: unless = if you don't

examples.en: If you eat these foods, you'll get a quick energy lift.
examples.why: a likely result of eating sugary food

examples.en: If you have a lot of food before exercise, you'll probably get a stomach ache!
examples.why: 'probably' softens the result, the pattern stays the same

grammar.watch: 'Unless' already means 'if … not', so don't make the verb after it negative.

words.title: Food and nutrition

items.def: A substance in food that provides the body with energy.
items.example: Eat healthy carbohydrates like wholemeal bread, pasta and brown rice.
items.example_vi: Hãy ăn tinh bột lành mạnh như bánh mì nguyên cám, mì ống và gạo lứt.

items.def: Substances you need to live and grow.
items.example: Your blood cells carry nutrients and oxygen to your muscles.
items.example_vi: Các tế bào máu mang chất dinh dưỡng và ô-xy tới cơ bắp của bạn.

items.def: A chemical you need to live and breathe.
items.example: You breathe faster during exercise because your muscles need more oxygen.
items.example_vi: Bạn thở gấp hơn khi tập luyện vì cơ bắp cần nhiều ô-xy hơn.

items.def: To change food so your body can use it.
items.example: A banana is easy to digest before you do sport.
items.example_vi: Quả chuối rất dễ tiêu hoá trước khi bạn chơi thể thao.

items.def: A substance in food that repairs your muscles and helps you get stronger.
items.example: Chicken, fish, eggs and lentils are good protein foods.
items.example_vi: Thịt gà, cá, trứng và đậu lăng là những món giàu chất đạm.

items.def: A substance that gives you strong bones.
items.example: Milk and yoghurt contain calcium to give you strong bones.
items.example_vi: Sữa và sữa chua có canxi giúp xương chắc khoẻ.

items.def: Having enough water in your body.
items.example: If you drink plenty of water, you'll stay cool and hydrated.
items.example_vi: Nếu bạn uống đủ nước, bạn sẽ mát mẻ và không bị thiếu nước.

words.note: Activity 6 asks you to find more 1st conditional sentences among these food tips.

readings.title: Tips for health and energy!
readings.about: Top athletes pay as much attention to what they eat as to how they train. The article explains carbohydrates, protein, calcium and water, and warns about sugary food.

summary.big_en: Warming up gets your body ready for sport, and need, should and mustn't turn that into clear instructions.

grammar.title: need / should / mustn't for advice and instructions
grammar.when: Use need when something is necessary, should to give advice, and mustn't to give strong advice against something.
grammar.form: subject + need to / should / mustn't + base verb

examples.en: First, we need to get your heart pumping.
examples.why: need = this is necessary

examples.en: You should warm up your hips too.
examples.why: should = advice, a good idea

examples.en: You mustn't start running without warming up your leg muscles.
examples.why: mustn't = strong advice against doing it

grammar.watch: 'Mustn't' is not the same as 'don't need to': mustn't means don't do it, don't need to means it isn't necessary.

items.def: The joint between your foot and your leg.
items.example: Rotate your ankle slowly ten times in each direction.
items.example_vi: Hãy xoay cổ chân thật chậm mười vòng mỗi chiều.

items.def: The joint where your arm joins your body.
items.example: Turn your shoulders in big circles to warm up your upper body.
items.example_vi: Xoay vai thành vòng lớn để khởi động phần thân trên.

items.def: The top part of your leg, above the knee.
items.example: Running uses the big muscles in your thighs.
items.example_vi: Chạy bộ dùng đến những cơ lớn ở đùi.

items.def: A muscle at the back of your thigh.
items.example: Stretch your hamstrings before you sprint.
items.example_vi: Hãy giãn cơ gân kheo trước khi chạy nước rút.

items.def: The joint where your leg joins your body.
items.example: You should warm up your hips too.
items.example_vi: Bạn cũng nên khởi động phần hông.

items.def: The joint in the middle of your leg.
items.example: Bend your knees a little before you jump.
items.example_vi: Hãy hơi khuỵu gối trước khi bật nhảy.

items.def: The five parts at the end of your foot.
items.example: Stand up straight and try to touch your toes.
items.example_vi: Đứng thẳng người rồi cố chạm vào các ngón chân.

items.def: The organ that pumps blood around your body.
items.example: First, we need to get your heart pumping.
items.example_vi: Trước tiên, chúng ta cần làm cho tim đập nhanh lên.

readings.title: Sam's warm-up instructions
readings.about: Sam gives instructions for a set of warm-up exercises. You put the pictures in order and say which parts of the body each exercise warms up.

summary.big_en: A biography tells a life story with dates, numbers and a quote, using the past simple for finished events and the present perfect for what the person has achieved.

grammar.title: Past simple and present perfect in a biography
grammar.when: Use the past simple for finished events, especially with a date; use the present perfect for achievements that count up to now.
grammar.form: past simple: verb + -ed / irregular form · present perfect: have / has + past participle

examples.en: Simone was born in Ohio, USA in 1997.
examples.why: past simple: a finished event with a date

examples.en: In 2014, she became the first woman in 40 years to win four gold medals.
examples.why: past simple again, because the year is given

examples.en: She has won more World Championship medals than any other man or woman.
examples.why: present perfect: the total counts up to today

examples.en: Simone has had setbacks in her journey to stardom, but she has never given up.
examples.why: present perfect for experience over a whole life so far

grammar.watch: Once you name the year, switch to the past simple: 'In 2011, she just missed being selected', not 'has missed'.

words.title: Talking about a sports star's life

items.def: A person who does gymnastics.
items.example: Simone Biles is the most successful gymnast of all time.
items.example_vi: Simone Biles là vận động viên thể dục dụng cụ thành công nhất mọi thời đại.

items.def: A natural ability to do something well.
items.example: A coach noticed her natural talent and invited her to join a class.
items.example_vi: Một huấn luyện viên nhận ra tài năng thiên bẩm của cô bé và mời cô vào lớp.

items.def: A person who trains a sports player or a team.
items.example: Her coach helped her to train for the World Championships.
items.example_vi: Huấn luyện viên đã giúp cô luyện tập cho Giải vô địch thế giới.

items.def: When a family looks after a child who is not their own.
items.example: She was in foster care until her grandparents adopted her.
items.example_vi: Cô sống ở gia đình chăm sóc tạm thời cho tới khi được ông bà nhận nuôi.

items.def: To laugh at someone in an unkind way.
items.example: In third grade, she was teased about her muscly legs.
items.example_vi: Hồi lớp ba, cô từng bị trêu chọc vì đôi chân nhiều cơ bắp.

items.def: To get better at something.
items.example: She used the experience to improve.
items.example_vi: Cô đã dùng trải nghiệm đó để tiến bộ hơn.

items.def: A problem that stops your progress for a while.
items.example: Missing the National team in 2011 was a big setback.
items.example_vi: Việc lỡ suất vào đội tuyển quốc gia năm 2011 là một trắc trở lớn.

items.def: To stop trying.
items.example: Simone has had setbacks, but she has never given up.
items.example_vi: Simone từng gặp trắc trở, nhưng cô chưa bao giờ bỏ cuộc.

readings.title: High flyer! A biography of Simone Biles
readings.about: The life of the gymnast Simone Biles, from foster care in Ohio to four gold medals and one bronze at the Rio Olympic Games. The four paragraphs cover her present-day success, her childhood, her early life and her journey to stardom.

summary.big_en: A commentator turns what he sees into words, choosing strong descriptive verbs and emphasising the key ones so the listener feels the excitement.

words.title: Football and match action

items.def: A person who describes a game while it is happening.
items.example: Danny acted as commentator so that his dad could follow the game.
items.example_vi: Danny làm bình luận viên để bố có thể theo dõi trận đấu.

items.def: A player whose job is to score goals.
items.example: The United defenders struggled to keep up with City's strikers.
items.example_vi: Các hậu vệ United chật vật theo kịp những tiền đạo của City.

items.def: A player whose job is to stop the other team scoring.
items.example: The ball ricocheted off a defender to Owusu.
items.example_vi: Quả bóng bật ra từ chân một hậu vệ tới chỗ Owusu.

items.def: The player who stands in the goal and stops shots.
items.example: He fired an unstoppable volley past the United keeper.
items.example_vi: Anh ấy tung cú vô-lê không thể cản phá qua thủ môn của United.

items.def: The middle part of a football pitch, between the two goals.
items.example: City's midfield dynamo launched a high cross into the United area.
items.example_vi: Nhạc trưởng tuyến giữa của City tạt một quả bổng vào vòng cấm United.

items.def: To kick or hit a ball before it touches the ground.
items.example: Owusu controlled the ball on his knee and volleyed it with amazing power.
items.example_vi: Owusu đỡ bóng bằng đầu gối rồi vô-lê với lực cực mạnh.

items.def: To kick or hit something very hard and fast.
items.example: He just blasted it in!
items.example_vi: Cậu ấy nã thẳng bóng vào lưới!

items.def: To jump high or a long way.
items.example: Danny and his dad leapt into each other's arms as the crowd exploded.
items.example_vi: Danny và bố nhảy cẫng lên ôm chầm lấy nhau khi khán đài vỡ oà.

words.note: Activity 7 asks you to replace plain words with these stronger ones: 'ran very fast' becomes 'blasted'.

sounds.title: Intonation: emphasising key words
sounds.focus: Listen for the words the commentator makes stand out. An emphasised word is said louder, longer and on a slightly higher note than the words around it; the small words in between are said quickly.
sounds.note: Emphasis changes how strongly you say a word, not the sounds inside it.

readings.title: Off Side by Tom Palmer
readings.about: Danny commentates a live City home game for his dad, who was blinded in an accident. Owusu scores with a powerful volley and Danny describes the goal again like a radio reporter.

summary.big_en: Emperor penguins survive the Antarctic winter by working together, and the present simple is how you describe things that are always true.

grammar.title: The present simple
grammar.when: Use the present simple to describe things that are always true, such as the life cycles of animals.
grammar.form: subject + base verb (add -s for he / she / it)

examples.en: The babies are a month old now. Soon they start to feed themselves.
examples.why: a stage of the life cycle, true every year

examples.en: The chicks stay balanced on their mother's feet.
examples.why: plural subject, so no -s on the verb

examples.en: Summer arrives and the chicks are almost fully grown.
examples.why: 'summer' is he / she / it, so the verb takes -s

examples.en: The babies gather together for protection.
examples.why: what these animals always do, not what happened once

grammar.watch: Don't switch to the past simple for a life cycle: penguins huddle every winter, not just last winter.

items.def: A baby bird.
items.example: The chicks stay balanced on their mother's feet.
items.example_vi: Những chú chim non đứng thăng bằng trên chân mẹ.

items.def: When an egg breaks and a young bird comes out.
items.example: Daylight appears again and thousands of chicks hatch.
items.example_vi: Ánh sáng ban ngày quay trở lại và hàng nghìn chim non nở ra.

items.def: To produce young animals.
items.example: Emperor penguins breed in the coldest place on Earth.
items.example_vi: Chim cánh cụt hoàng đế sinh sản ở nơi lạnh nhất Trái Đất.

items.def: An animal's partner, for producing young.
items.example: Each penguin finds a mate before the long winter begins.
items.example_vi: Mỗi con chim cánh cụt tìm một bạn đời trước khi mùa đông dài bắt đầu.

items.def: To stand very close together to keep warm.
items.example: The penguins huddle together when the freezing wind blows.
items.example_vi: Đàn chim cánh cụt xúm sát vào nhau khi gió lạnh buốt thổi tới.

items.def: A group of birds that live together.
items.example: Emperor penguins live in a huge colony on the ice.
items.example_vi: Chim cánh cụt hoàng đế sống thành một quần thể khổng lồ trên mặt băng.

items.def: To stay alive in difficult conditions.
items.example: Penguin families survive the extreme cold of Antarctica.
items.example_vi: Các gia đình chim cánh cụt sống sót qua cái lạnh khắc nghiệt ở Nam Cực.

readings.title: Emperor penguins (documentary)
readings.about: A documentary in two parts about how emperor penguin families raise their chicks. Part 2 follows the chicks from hatching to the summer, when they are almost fully grown.

summary.big_en: Every animal depends on a food chain that starts with a plant, and relative clauses let you add the important details about each link.

grammar.title: Defining relative clauses
grammar.when: A defining relative clause gives important information about a person, animal or thing, so the reader knows exactly which one you mean.
grammar.form: noun + relative pronoun (who, which, that, whose, where, when) + clause

examples.en: These creatures are small carnivores whose main diet is meat.
examples.why: whose = the diet belongs to the carnivores

examples.en: Primary consumers are creatures who only eat plants.
examples.why: who introduces the clause about living creatures

examples.en: There are also consumers whose food comes from plants and meat.
examples.why: whose again, showing what belongs to them

examples.en: The top predators who are at the top of the food chain have no natural enemies.
examples.why: the clause tells you which predators are meant

grammar.watch: Use who for people and animals, which or that for things, and whose to show that something belongs to someone.

words.title: Food chains and feeding

items.def: A living thing that makes its own food; every food chain starts with one.
items.example: The plant is called a producer because it makes its own food from the sun.
items.example_vi: Cây được gọi là sinh vật sản xuất vì nó tự tạo ra thức ăn từ ánh nắng.

items.def: A living thing that gets its food by eating other living things.
items.example: The next link in the food chain is called a consumer.
items.example_vi: Mắt xích tiếp theo trong chuỗi thức ăn được gọi là sinh vật tiêu thụ.

items.def: An animal that only eats plants.
items.example: Rabbits, mice and grasshoppers are herbivores.
items.example_vi: Thỏ, chuột và châu chấu là những loài ăn cỏ.

items.def: An animal whose main diet is meat.
items.example: Frogs, lizards and spiders are small carnivores.
items.example_vi: Ếch, thằn lằn và nhện là những loài ăn thịt cỡ nhỏ.

items.def: An animal that eats both plants and meat.
items.example: An omnivore can be a secondary or a tertiary consumer.
items.example_vi: Loài ăn tạp có thể là sinh vật tiêu thụ bậc hai hoặc bậc ba.

items.def: An animal that hunts and eats other animals.
items.example: Top predators like lions and sharks have no natural enemies.
items.example_vi: Những kẻ săn mồi đầu bảng như sư tử và cá mập không có kẻ thù tự nhiên.

items.def: The way living things affect each other and the environment.
items.example: All animals and plants are important in our planet's ecosystem.
items.example_vi: Mọi loài động vật và thực vật đều quan trọng trong hệ sinh thái của hành tinh.

items.def: The food and drink that a living thing needs.
items.example: These creatures are carnivores whose main diet is meat.
items.example_vi: Những sinh vật này là loài ăn thịt, thức ăn chính của chúng là thịt.

items.def: The natural place where an animal or a plant lives.
items.example: The polar bear's habitat is the ice around the North Pole.
items.example_vi: Môi trường sống của gấu Bắc Cực là vùng băng quanh Bắc Cực.

words.note: Activity 3 asks you to order Algae, Krill, Squid, Seal and Polar bear into one food chain.

readings.title: Nature's food chains
readings.about: An explanation of how a food chain works: the plant producer, the three levels of consumer, and the top predators with no natural enemies.

summary.big_en: Wh- questions are the quickest way to find out key facts, such as where carnivorous plants grow and how they catch their prey.

grammar.title: Wh- questions review
grammar.when: Use a wh- question when you want a fact, not a yes or a no.
grammar.form: question word + do / does + subject + verb

examples.en: What do you know about carnivorous plants?
examples.why: the model in the Use of English box

examples.en: Where do carnivorous plants grow?
examples.why: plural subject, so 'do'

examples.en: Why do these plants eat other living things?
examples.why: 'why' asks for a reason

examples.en: How does a carnivorous plant catch its prey?
examples.why: singular subject, so 'does' and the verb stays 'catch'

grammar.watch: After do or does the verb goes back to its base form: 'How does it catch…?', not 'How does it catches…?'

words.title: Carnivorous plants and how they trap prey

items.def: Meat-eating; a carnivorous plant eats insects and other small animals.
items.example: Where do carnivorous plants grow?
items.example_vi: Cây ăn thịt mọc ở đâu?

items.def: An animal that another living thing catches and eats.
items.example: How does a carnivorous plant catch its prey?
items.example_vi: Cây ăn thịt bắt con mồi bằng cách nào?

items.def: A very thin thread that grows on skin, or on the leaf of a plant.
items.example: The Sundew plant has long thin leaves covered in tiny hairs.
items.example_vi: Cây gọng vó có những chiếc lá dài mảnh phủ đầy lông tơ.

items.def: Holding on to whatever it touches.
items.example: The insect is held by the thick sticky liquid on the leaf.
items.example_vi: Con côn trùng bị giữ lại bởi lớp chất lỏng dính đặc trên lá.

items.def: Something that flows, like water.
items.example: The leaves are covered in a thick sticky liquid.
items.example_vi: Những chiếc lá phủ đầy một lớp chất lỏng dính đặc.

items.def: To catch something so that it cannot escape.
items.example: When an insect crawls onto the leaves, it is trapped.
items.example_vi: Khi một con côn trùng bò lên lá, nó bị mắc bẫy.

items.def: To press something so hard that it breaks.
items.example: Then the leaf curls around the insect and crushes it.
items.example_vi: Sau đó chiếc lá cuộn lại quanh con côn trùng và nghiền nát nó.

items.def: To make something break down in a liquid.
items.example: The juices of the plant slowly dissolve the insect.
items.example_vi: Dịch của cây từ từ làm tan rã con côn trùng.

sounds.title: Intonation in question forms
sounds.focus: Listen to where the voice goes at the end of the question. In a wh- question the voice usually falls on the last important word; in a yes / no question it rises instead.
sounds.note: The question word itself is said clearly, but the fall happens at the end: 'Where do carnivorous plants GROW↘?'

readings.title: Minh explains carnivorous plants
readings.about: Minh answers four questions about carnivorous plants, then explains how the Sundew traps an insect on its sticky leaves and crushes it.

summary.big_en: An infographic gives the most important facts about a type of animal in short present simple sentences next to clear images.

grammar.title: Present simple and relative clauses in an infographic
grammar.when: An infographic states facts that are always true, so use the present simple, keep sentences short, and use a defining relative clause to say exactly which animals you mean.
grammar.form: short present simple sentence · noun + which / who + clause

examples.en: Amphibians are animals which can live in water and on land.
examples.why: 'which can live…' says which animals count as amphibians

examples.en: They need a moist environment to survive.
examples.why: present simple for a fact that is always true

examples.en: Most amphibians have lungs and gills.
examples.why: a short sentence with one clear fact

examples.en: Amphibians lay their eggs in water.
examples.why: present simple for a life cycle

grammar.watch: Keep the facts general: 'Amphibians lay their eggs in water', not 'This frog laid its eggs yesterday'.

words.title: Animal types and body parts

items.def: An animal which can live in water and on land.
items.example: Frogs, toads, salamanders and newts are amphibians.
items.example_vi: Ếch, cóc, kỳ giông và sa giông là động vật lưỡng cư.

items.def: An animal that has a spine, or back bone.
items.example: Amphibians are vertebrates, which means they have a back bone.
items.example_vi: Động vật lưỡng cư là động vật có xương sống, nghĩa là chúng có cột sống.

items.def: A little bit wet.
items.example: Amphibians need a moist environment to survive.
items.example_vi: Động vật lưỡng cư cần môi trường ẩm ướt để sống.

items.def: The parts a fish or a young amphibian uses to breathe under water.
items.example: Most amphibians have lungs and gills.
items.example_vi: Phần lớn động vật lưỡng cư có cả phổi lẫn mang.

items.def: The two organs in the chest that an animal breathes with.
items.example: When they develop legs and lungs, they move onto the land.
items.example_vi: Khi mọc chân và có phổi, chúng chuyển lên cạn để sống.

items.def: Small hard plates that cover the skin of a fish or a reptile.
items.example: The chameleon has scales but the whale has smooth skin.
items.example_vi: Tắc kè hoa có vảy còn cá voi thì da trơn nhẵn.

items.def: The flat parts a fish uses to swim.
items.example: A fish uses its fins to push itself through the water.
items.example_vi: Cá dùng vây để đẩy mình đi trong nước.

items.def: The light soft parts that cover a bird's body.
items.example: Birds are the only animals with feathers.
items.example_vi: Chim là loài động vật duy nhất có lông vũ.

words.note: Activity 2 asks you to match these words to insects, fish, mammals, amphibians, birds and reptiles.

readings.title: What is an amphibian?
readings.about: An infographic about amphibians: their habitat, their skin and breathing, their eggs and life cycle, and the bright colours that warn other animals away.

summary.big_en: Blue 55 sings at a frequency no other whale understands, and Iris, who is deaf, knows exactly how that feels.

grammar.title: Collective nouns
grammar.when: Use a collective noun to name a group of specific things, especially a group of animals.
grammar.form: a + collective noun + of + plural noun

examples.en: A pod of whales.
examples.why: the example in the Language focus box

examples.en: A herd of elephants.
examples.why: large animals that move together

examples.en: A pack of wolves.
examples.why: animals that hunt together

examples.en: A flock of birds.
examples.why: birds flying or feeding together

examples.en: A pride of lions.
examples.why: the family group of lions

grammar.watch: Each animal has its own collective noun, so you can't say 'a pod of lions' or 'a pride of whales'.

items.def: A very large area of sea.
items.example: The video started out with a whale swimming in the ocean.
items.example_vi: Đoạn phim mở đầu bằng cảnh một con cá voi bơi giữa đại dương.

items.def: A group of whales.
items.example: Blue 55 swam around by himself and not in a pod.
items.example_vi: Blue 55 bơi một mình chứ không đi theo đàn.

items.def: Very small plants and animals that bigger sea animals eat.
items.example: Baleen whales eat plankton and small fish.
items.example_vi: Cá voi tấm sừng ăn sinh vật phù du và cá nhỏ.

items.def: A group of animals that are very similar.
items.example: The skin sample showed that his parents had been different species.
items.example_vi: Mẫu da cho thấy bố mẹ của nó thuộc hai loài khác nhau.

items.def: A mixture of two very different things.
items.example: Blue 55 is a hybrid: his mother was a blue whale and his father a fin whale.
items.example_vi: Blue 55 là một con lai: mẹ nó là cá voi xanh còn bố là cá voi vây.

items.def: A scientist who studies sea life.
items.example: Marine biologists figured out why the whale was all alone in the ocean.
items.example_vi: Các nhà sinh vật biển đã tìm ra vì sao con cá voi lại lẻ loi giữa đại dương.

items.def: When animals travel to a different place.
items.example: The researchers wanted to follow his migration pattern.
items.example_vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu muốn theo dõi lộ trình di cư của nó.

items.def: A safe place for animals.
items.example: Researchers from a marine sanctuary tried to put a tracker on him.
items.example_vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu từ một khu bảo tồn biển đã thử gắn thiết bị theo dõi lên nó.

readings.title: Song for a Whale by Lynne Kelly
readings.about: Iris, a deaf girl, watches a class video about Blue 55, a hybrid whale who calls at around fifty-five hertz instead of thirty-five, so no other whale understands him. She recognises her own loneliness in his story.

summary.big_en: Everyone has a favourite gadget, and you explain your choice by saying what you use it for and comparing it with something else.

words.title: Gadgets and equipment

items.def: A small useful tool or machine.
items.example: What is your favourite gadget or piece of equipment?
items.example_vi: Món đồ công nghệ hay dụng cụ nào em thích nhất?

items.def: The things you need in order to do an activity.
items.example: My mountain bike is the most important piece of equipment for me.
items.example_vi: Chiếc xe đạp địa hình là dụng cụ quan trọng nhất với em.

items.def: A small flat computer with a touch screen.
items.example: It's got to be my tablet – I can't live without it!
items.example_vi: Chắc chắn là chiếc máy tính bảng của em – em không sống thiếu nó được!

items.def: A machine or tool made to do a particular job.
items.example: A tablet is a device you can use to go online and message your friends.
items.example_vi: Máy tính bảng là thiết bị em có thể dùng để vào mạng và nhắn tin cho bạn bè.

items.def: Something good about a thing; a reason it helps you.
items.example: Name two advantages and one disadvantage of each gadget.
items.example_vi: Hãy nêu hai ưu điểm và một nhược điểm của mỗi món đồ.

items.def: Something bad about a thing; a problem with it.
items.example: One disadvantage of a mountain bike is that you can't use it in the rain.
items.example_vi: Một nhược điểm của xe đạp địa hình là em không dùng được khi trời mưa.

items.def: To have a particular heaviness.
items.example: In 1973 this gadget was 22 centimetres long and weighed 1.13 kilograms.
items.example_vi: Năm 1973, món đồ này dài 22 xăng-ti-mét và nặng 1,13 ki-lô-gam.

words.note: Activity 2 is a quiz: you match six clues about famous gadgets to six pictures.

groups.when: Naming your choice and your reason
lines: It's got to be my… because I can use it to…
The most important gadget for me is… because…
I think it's more useful than a…
I think it's… than a… because…
That's true, but…

readings.title: Lucia and Ben talk about their favourite gadgets
readings.about: Two children each describe a favourite gadget or piece of equipment and give two advantages and one disadvantage of it.

summary.big_en: The story of the Asimo robot is told in the past simple, because every step of it comes with a date.

grammar.title: Past simple review
grammar.when: Use the past simple for finished actions in the past. We often say exactly when they happened.
grammar.form: subject + verb + -ed (regular) or the irregular past form, + a time reference

examples.en: Scientists started developing Asimo in the 1980s.
examples.why: start + -ed, with the time reference 'in the 1980s'

examples.en: In 2014 it played football with the former US president.
examples.why: play + -ed, with the time reference 'in 2014'

examples.en: In 2005, Mickey Mouse welcomed Asimo at Disneyland.
examples.why: the form is the same for every subject

examples.en: In 2018, Honda stopped producing the robot in its current form.
examples.why: stop doubles the p before -ed

grammar.watch: Say when it happened and you need the past simple ('presented it to the world in 2000'); leave the time out and the text switches to the present perfect ('Since then, scientists have upgraded Asimo's technology').

words.title: Design technology

items.def: Like a human.
items.example: Asimo is the most advanced humanoid robot in the world.
items.example_vi: Asimo là robot hình người tiên tiến nhất thế giới.

items.def: A device that detects objects nearby.
items.example: Asimo moves by itself using sensors inside its body.
items.example_vi: Asimo tự di chuyển nhờ các cảm biến bên trong cơ thể.

items.def: A device that produces electricity.
items.example: Asimo is just over one metre tall and has a rechargeable battery.
items.example_vi: Asimo cao hơn một mét một chút và có pin sạc lại được.

items.def: To change something to make it better.
items.example: Scientists have upgraded Asimo's technology, so it has more skills.
items.example_vi: Các nhà khoa học đã nâng cấp công nghệ của Asimo nên nó có thêm nhiều kỹ năng.

items.def: An order telling a person or machine what to do.
items.example: It can understand voice commands and human gestures.
items.example_vi: Nó hiểu được khẩu lệnh và cử chỉ của con người.

items.def: A movement of the hands or head that means something.
items.example: Asimo recognises human gestures as well as moving objects.
items.example_vi: Asimo nhận ra cử chỉ của con người và cả những vật đang chuyển động.

words.note: humanoid, sensor, battery and upgrade are the book's Key words box for design technology (p.64).

readings.title: Meet Asimo, the most advanced humanoid robot in the world
readings.about: Asimo walks on two legs, understands voice commands and gestures, and can pour a drink. Honda started it in the 1980s, showed it to the world in 2000 and stopped making it in 2018.

summary.big_en: When you present a new invention, will and won't are how you tell your audience what it is going to do for them.

grammar.title: will for future predictions
grammar.when: Use will and won't to predict what is going to happen in the future.
grammar.form: will / won't + plain verb (no 'to'); the form never changes with I, you, he, she, it, we, they

examples.en: This invention will change the way people travel.
examples.why: will + plain verb, no 'to' and no ending

examples.en: People won't crash into each other.
examples.why: won't is the short form of will not

examples.en: Which idea will the judges choose?
examples.why: question form: will comes before the subject

examples.en: You will be able to travel as fast as you like.
examples.why: 'be able to' is what follows will when you mean 'can'

grammar.watch: Never put 'to' after will: 'It will save money', not 'It will to save money'.

items.def: Something completely new that somebody has made.
items.example: Kim gave a presentation about her idea for a new invention.
items.example_vi: Kim thuyết trình về ý tưởng cho một phát minh mới.

items.def: The people who listen to or watch you.
items.example: Think about who your audience is before you plan your presentation.
items.example_vi: Hãy nghĩ xem người nghe của em là ai trước khi lên kế hoạch thuyết trình.

items.def: A person who decides who wins a competition.
items.example: Which idea will the judges choose?
items.example_vi: Ban giám khảo sẽ chọn ý tưởng nào?

items.def: To find an answer to a problem.
items.example: Uber Jet Boots will solve the traffic problems in our city.
items.example_vi: Giày phản lực Uber sẽ giải quyết vấn đề giao thông ở thành phố chúng ta.

items.def: A short repeat of the main points at the end.
items.example: A summary of the idea comes at the end of the presentation.
items.example_vi: Phần tóm tắt ý tưởng nằm ở cuối bài thuyết trình.

items.def: Having a lot of force or strength.
items.example: The jet will be so powerful that you can stand up straight.
items.example_vi: Luồng phản lực sẽ mạnh đến mức em có thể đứng thẳng người.

readings.title: Kim's presentation: the Uber Jet Boots
readings.about: Kim shows a picture, describes her idea for jet boots and says how people will use them. Afterwards the audience asks how you get on the boots and where the power comes from.

summary.big_en: A persuasive essay puts your opinion first, then backs it up with reasons and examples, strongest reason first.

items.def: What you yourself think about something.
items.example: In my opinion, the most important invention of all time is the wheel.
items.example_vi: Theo em, phát minh quan trọng nhất mọi thời đại là bánh xe.

items.def: Why you think something; what makes it true.
items.example: Start your essay with your strongest reason.
items.example_vi: Hãy mở đầu bài luận bằng lý do thuyết phục nhất của em.

items.def: Good at making people agree with you.
items.example: The aim of a persuasive essay is to make the reader agree with you.
items.example_vi: Mục đích của bài luận thuyết phục là khiến người đọc đồng ý với em.

items.def: To need something in order to manage.
items.example: We depend on the wheel for all our transport.
items.example_vi: Chúng ta phụ thuộc vào bánh xe cho mọi phương tiện đi lại.

items.def: Working well without wasting time or effort.
items.example: Carrying heavy things without wheels isn't very fast or efficient.
items.example_vi: Mang vác đồ nặng mà không có bánh xe thì không nhanh và không hiệu quả.

items.def: How far it is between two places.
items.example: It is very difficult to travel long distances without wheels.
items.example_vi: Đi những quãng đường dài mà không có bánh xe thì rất khó.

items.def: A wheel with teeth that makes a machine turn.
items.example: The wheels that make machines in factories work are called cogs.
items.example_vi: Những bánh xe làm cho máy móc trong nhà máy hoạt động được gọi là bánh răng.

lines: In my opinion, …
I think that…
This is because we need wheels to travel…
We need the wheel so people can work easily.
…because planes need wheels to take off.
…such as cars, trains and planes.
…for example, by themselves or using animals.

groups.when: Describing an invention without naming it
lines: People need this invention so they can…
Without this invention, it is very difficult to… This means that…

readings.title: A world without wheels, by Hassan
readings.about: Hassan argues that the wheel is the most important invention ever, because without it we could not travel far or carry heavy things easily. He ends by pointing out that machines in factories and on farms need wheels called cogs.

summary.big_en: Garth's story shows that a good idea is still a good idea even when other people laugh at it.

grammar.title: Multi-word verbs
grammar.when: A multi-word verb has two parts, and together they often mean something different from the verb on its own.
grammar.form: verb + preposition or adverb

examples.en: …he could hardly wait to try it out.
examples.why: try out = test something to see if it works

examples.en: Garth turned quickly to run back home.
examples.why: run back = go back the way you came

examples.en: The three boys ran off shrieking with laughter.
examples.why: run off = leave quickly

examples.en: Don't let stupid ignorant boys like that put you down!
examples.why: put down = make someone feel small

grammar.watch: The object can come between the two parts: 'he tried it out', 'she held it up'.

words.title: Words from the story

items.def: A person who makes something completely new.
items.example: The lady wanted to find the best young inventor in the town.
items.example_vi: Người phụ nữ muốn tìm ra nhà phát minh nhỏ tuổi giỏi nhất thị trấn.

items.def: Clear, so you can see through it.
items.example: Garth's design covered his head in a magnificent transparent dome.
items.example_vi: Thiết kế của Garth trùm lên đầu cậu một mái vòm trong suốt tuyệt đẹp.

items.def: To look at someone in a cruel way.
items.example: Todd sneered at Garth and said the Bodybrella looked dumb.
items.example_vi: Todd cười khinh Garth và bảo chiếc Bodybrella trông thật ngớ ngẩn.

items.def: Cruel comments.
items.example: The mocking jibes rang in Garth's ears long after the boys had gone.
items.example_vi: Những lời chế giễu cay độc còn vang bên tai Garth rất lâu sau khi mấy cậu kia đi khỏi.

items.def: Feeling stupid in front of other people.
items.example: Trembling and humiliated, Garth picked up his battered invention.
items.example_vi: Run rẩy và tủi hổ, Garth nhặt phát minh đã móp méo của mình lên.

items.def: Horrible, disgusting.
items.example: Maybe the repugnant Todd Barker was right after all.
items.example_vi: Có lẽ tên Todd Barker đáng ghét ấy nói đúng thật.

items.def: A paper or card you use instead of money in a shop.
items.example: Each of the three winners will get a big voucher to spend on gadgets.
items.example_vi: Mỗi người trong ba người thắng cuộc sẽ nhận một phiếu mua hàng lớn để mua đồ công nghệ.

words.note: sneer, jibes, humiliated and repugnant are the two Glossary boxes on pages 71 and 72.

sounds.title: The two sounds of the letter 'a'
sounds.focus: The same letter 'a' is said two different ways in these story words. In lady, okay, able, display and place it is the long /eɪ/ sound, the same as the name of the letter. In strap, hands, gadget, bag and have it is the short /æ/ sound.
sounds.note: A silent -e at the end usually gives you the long sound: place /pleɪs/ but bag /bæɡ/.

readings.title: Start Small, Think Big, by Jane Boylan
readings.about: Garth proudly tests his Bodybrella in the rain until the Barker Boys break it and laugh at him. A lady who owns a gadget shop then admires his idea and invites him to enter her competition for young inventors.

summary.big_en: How people choose to spend money says a lot about them, and comparative adverbs are how you compare the way things are done.

grammar.title: Comparative adverbs
grammar.when: Use comparative adverbs with verbs to show a change, or to compare how something is done.
grammar.form: more / less + adverb (more easily, less quickly); short adverbs just add -er (longer, faster, harder)

examples.en: The expensive brands are made better…
examples.why: better is the irregular comparative of well

examples.en: …he grows out of them less quickly than me.
examples.why: less + adverb makes the opposite comparison

examples.en: If something is made well, it usually lasts longer.
examples.why: long is short, so it takes -er, not 'more long'

examples.en: I can save my pocket money more easily if I don't go shopping!
examples.why: easily ends in -ly, so it takes 'more'

grammar.watch: The adverb of 'good' is 'well', and its comparative is 'better' – never 'more well'.

words.title: Money words

items.def: Spending money on something that isn't useful.
items.example: It's a waste of money to buy trainers you never wear.
items.example_vi: Mua giày thể thao mà chẳng bao giờ đi là phí tiền.

items.def: To have enough money to buy something.
items.example: Should you buy the most expensive tablet you can afford?
items.example_vi: Em có nên mua chiếc máy tính bảng đắt nhất mà em đủ tiền mua không?

items.def: To continue to be in good condition.
items.example: If something is made well, it usually lasts longer.
items.example_vi: Nếu một món đồ được làm tốt thì thường bền lâu hơn.

items.def: An organisation that provides money and help.
items.example: I'd give the money to a charity that helps animals and wildlife.
items.example_vi: Em sẽ tặng số tiền đó cho một tổ chức từ thiện giúp đỡ động vật hoang dã.

items.def: To keep money so you can use it in the future.
items.example: I save some of my pocket money for something special.
items.example_vi: Em để dành một phần tiền tiêu vặt cho một thứ đặc biệt.

items.def: A type of product made by a particular company.
items.example: The expensive brands are made better than the cheap ones.
items.example_vi: Những thương hiệu đắt tiền được làm tốt hơn loại rẻ.

words.note: These six are the words you match to definitions in Activity 6 (p.79).

phrases.title: Giving your opinion about spending money

groups.when: Saying what is worth the money
lines: It's better to spend money on…
I'd buy a… because…

groups.when: Saying what is not worth the money
lines: It's a waste of money to…
If you buy a new tablet, you should buy…

readings.title: Friends discussing expensive trainers
readings.about: Some friends argue about one of the quiz questions and give two reasons for buying expensive trainers and two reasons against.

summary.big_en: Turning a money-raising idea into real numbers means adding up your costs, taking them off your sales and seeing what profit is left.

grammar.title: Quantifiers
grammar.when: Quantifiers say how much or how many. Use several and plenty of when you don't know the exact amount; either… or and both of always talk about two things.
grammar.form: several / plenty of + plural noun; either… or…; both of + these / the + plural noun

examples.en: There are several ways you can make chocolate treats.
examples.why: several = a smaller amount, about 3 or 4

examples.en: Plenty of people agreed – we sold 95% of our brownies.
examples.why: plenty of = lots of

examples.en: All profits will go to two charities, either Polar Bear Rescue or Global Welfare.
examples.why: either… or… = one of two

examples.en: Both of these charities do amazing work to help our planet.
examples.why: both of = the two of them together

grammar.watch: Don't swap them round: plenty of means lots, several means only about three or four.

words.title: Calculations and money

items.def: The amount of money needed for something.
items.example: Can you calculate the total cost of the ingredients?
items.example_vi: Em có tính được tổng chi phí nguyên liệu không?

items.def: An amount of something out of 100.
items.example: Ava and Alex sold 95 percent of their brownies.
items.example_vi: Ava và Alex đã bán được 95 phần trăm số bánh brownie.

items.def: A unit of weight; 1,000 grams.
items.example: The recipe needs 1.1 kilograms of butter for 100 brownies.
items.example_vi: Công thức cần 1,1 ki-lô-gam bơ cho 100 chiếc bánh.

items.def: To work out an amount using numbers.
items.example: Calculate the new costs if you make 200 brownies.
items.example_vi: Hãy tính chi phí mới nếu em làm 200 chiếc bánh.

items.def: One of the foods you use to make a dish.
items.example: What are the new measurements for each ingredient?
items.example_vi: Định lượng mới cho mỗi nguyên liệu là bao nhiêu?

items.def: The money you have left after you take away your costs.
items.example: They sold all the brownies and made a profit of $80.00.
items.example_vi: Họ bán hết bánh và thu được lợi nhuận 80 đô la.

items.def: A part of a whole number, such as 1/2 or 1/5.
items.example: You can write 50% as the fraction 1/2.
items.example_vi: Em có thể viết 50% dưới dạng phân số 1/2.

words.note: cost, % (percent) and kg (kilogram) are the book's Key words box for calculations (p.80).

readings.title: Brownies2go: Ava and Alex's poster
readings.about: Ava and Alex list the ingredients and costs for 100 chocolate brownies, then sell 95 of them at $1.00 each at the community fair. After costs they are left with $80.00 profit, which they share between two charities.

summary.big_en: Deciding together how to spend a sum of money means introducing your point, suggesting, agreeing and sometimes only partly agreeing.

words.title: Talking about raising and spending money

items.def: To collect money by doing an activity.
items.example: Have you ever done activities to raise money for charity?
items.example_vi: Em đã bao giờ làm hoạt động để quyên tiền cho từ thiện chưa?

items.def: The money that a country uses.
items.example: How much is $825 US in the currency of your country?
items.example_vi: 825 đô la Mỹ bằng bao nhiêu theo tiền tệ nước em?

items.def: An idea you offer for other people to think about.
items.example: What suggestion does Nacho make to the class?
items.example_vi: Nacho đưa ra đề xuất gì cho cả lớp?

items.def: A talk in which people share their ideas.
items.example: In a discussion, use phrases to introduce your points.
items.example_vi: Trong một cuộc thảo luận, hãy dùng các cụm từ để mở đầu ý của em.

items.def: To answer or react to what someone says.
items.example: Marina responds to Nacho's idea with an idea of her own.
items.example_vi: Marina đáp lại ý tưởng của Nacho bằng một ý tưởng của riêng cô ấy.

items.def: To talk with other people until you all agree.
items.example: When you negotiate, you make suggestions and listen to other people.
items.example_vi: Khi thương lượng, em đưa ra đề xuất và lắng nghe người khác.

lines: We think we should spend the money on…
How about spending it on our end-of-term celebration?
What about using a small amount of the money for…?
We agree with that.
We think it's a good idea to buy sports equipment, but not for the table tennis club.
What does everyone else think?

readings.title: The class discussion about the money they raised
readings.about: A class talks about how to spend the $825 they raised. Nacho makes a suggestion, his classmate Marina responds, and other classmates add ideas with reasons.

summary.big_en: An opinion essay needs connecting words to put the points in order, and reflexive pronouns to show who did something on their own.

grammar.title: Reflexive pronouns
grammar.when: Use a reflexive pronoun to draw attention to the person or people you are talking about, especially when they do something on their own.
grammar.form: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves

examples.en: Last year I saved and bought a video game myself.
examples.why: he did it on his own, with nobody's help

examples.en: …it teaches us to manage money ourselves.
examples.why: us becomes ourselves

examples.en: …when you buy things yourself, you learn about how much things cost.
examples.why: you becomes yourself

examples.en: I didn't know how expensive they were until I bought one for myself!
examples.why: after a preposition: for myself

grammar.watch: Plural forms end in -selves: ourselves, yourselves, themselves – never 'ourselfs'.

items.def: Money your family gives you to spend yourself.
items.example: Do you get pocket money from your family?
items.example_vi: Em có được gia đình cho tiền tiêu vặt không?

items.def: To understand how much something is really worth.
items.example: If you don't buy anything yourself, you don't appreciate the cost of things.
items.example_vi: Nếu không tự mua thứ gì, em sẽ không hiểu được giá trị của đồ vật.

items.def: To look after something carefully and keep control of it.
items.example: Pocket money teaches us to manage money ourselves.
items.example_vi: Tiền tiêu vặt dạy chúng em tự quản lý tiền bạc.

items.def: The amount of money you pay for something.
items.example: It makes you compare prices and find ways to buy things more cheaply.
items.example_vi: Nó khiến em so sánh giá cả và tìm cách mua đồ rẻ hơn.

items.def: Costing a lot of money.
items.example: I didn't know how expensive video games were until I bought one.
items.example_vi: Em không biết trò chơi điện tử đắt đến thế cho tới khi tự mua một cái.

items.def: The last part of an essay, which sums up the main point.
items.example: The conclusion of Ismail's essay summarises his main point.
items.example_vi: Phần kết luận trong bài luận của Ismail tóm tắt lại ý chính.

phrases.title: Connecting words in an opinion essay

lines: In my opinion, children should have pocket money…

groups.when: Showing the order of your points
lines: Firstly, when you have pocket money you learn how to spend money in a good way.
Secondly, when you buy things yourself, you learn about how much things cost.
Finally, I think pocket money is a very good idea because…
…because it teaches us useful things about money.
Children already have everything they need, therefore they don't need pocket money.
However, some parents say that children already have everything they need.
But, if you don't buy anything yourself, you don't appreciate the cost of things.

readings.title: Should children get pocket money? – Ismail's essay
readings.about: Eleven-year-old Ismail argues that children should get pocket money because it teaches them to spend well, to know what things cost and to manage money themselves. He also answers one point against his opinion.

summary.big_en: Joe Spud's father can buy him anything in the world, which is exactly why the one present Joe really wants cannot be bought.

words.title: Words from the story

items.def: Someone who has more than a thousand million pounds or dollars.
items.example: 'You are a billionaire, boy,' said Mr Spud.
items.example_vi: 'Con là tỉ phú mà, con trai,' ông Spud nói.

items.def: A type of servant who works in a big house.
items.example: For a while they had a butler called Otis who was also an orang-utan.
items.example_vi: Có một dạo nhà họ có một quản gia tên Otis, mà lại là một con đười ươi.

items.def: A special glass for drinks.
items.example: He and his dad drank orange squash from priceless antique goblets.
items.example_vi: Cậu và bố uống nước cam từ những chiếc ly cổ vô giá.

items.def: Expensive and meant for rich people.
items.example: 'I can afford to send you to the poshest schools in the world.'
items.example_vi: 'Bố đủ tiền cho con học những trường sang trọng nhất thế giới.'

items.def: Looking sad and alone.
items.example: Mr Spud looked forlorn because there was nothing left to buy his son.
items.example_vi: Ông Spud trông buồn thiu vì chẳng còn gì để mua cho con trai nữa.

items.def: The angry feeling you get when you can't have what you want.
items.example: 'Boring! Boring! Boring!' Joe stamped his feet in frustration.
items.example_vi: 'Chán ngắt! Chán ngắt! Chán ngắt!' Joe giậm chân bực bội.

items.def: Not real; made to look like the real thing.
items.example: In the grounds there was a ski-slope with mountains of fake snow.
items.example_vi: Trong khuôn viên có một dốc trượt tuyết với những núi tuyết giả.

words.note: butler and goblet come from the Glossary on page 86; the others are the powerful words the author uses instead of ordinary ones.

sounds.title: The two sounds of the letter 's'
sounds.focus: The letter 's' has a soft sound /s/ and a hard sound /z/. It is /s/ at the start of a word (seven, solid, son) and at the end of house. It is /z/ between two vowels (visible) and in a plural -s that follows a voiced sound (handles, pounds, problems, mountains).
sounds.note: A plural -s is /z/ after a voiced sound, as in pounds /paʊndz/, but /s/ after an unvoiced one, as in gadgets /ˈɡædʒɪts/.

groups.when: Someone who has so much money they spend it carelessly
lines: He has more money than sense.
He has money to burn.

groups.when: A job that pays very little
lines: He has a job that pays peanuts.

readings.title: Billionaire Boy, by David Walliams
readings.about: Joe Spud lives in a huge house with gold taps, mink carpets and an orang-utan butler, but for his birthday the only present he really wants is a friend. He asks his dad to let him leave his expensive school and go to the local comp instead.

summary.big_en: People often end up in a job that grew out of something they were good at or keen on at school. Compound nouns and adjective + preposition phrases are the tools for talking about it.

grammar.title: Compound nouns
grammar.when: Use a compound noun when two words work together as one name for a thing or a person.
grammar.form: noun or adjective (describes) + noun

examples.en: She is a marine biologist.
examples.why: marine describes biologist

examples.en: We watched a wildlife documentary about penguins.
examples.why: wildlife describes documentary

examples.en: My science teacher used to be a computer programmer.
examples.why: two compound nouns, each written as two words

examples.en: He put the photos on his website.
examples.why: some compound nouns are written as one word

grammar.watch: The first word describes the second, and the second word is always the noun: a sports injury is a kind of injury, not a kind of sport.

grammar.title: Adjectives + prepositions + nouns
grammar.when: Some adjectives always take the same preposition, and a noun or an -ing word comes after it.
grammar.form: adjective + preposition + noun

examples.en: I was good at maths and science anyway.
examples.why: good always takes at

examples.en: I was always really keen on sport.
examples.why: keen always takes on

examples.en: I became more interested in coding.
examples.why: interested always takes in

examples.en: I was always fascinated by the ocean.
examples.why: fascinated always takes by

grammar.watch: Learn the adjective and its preposition together as one item: good at, keen on, interested in, fascinated by.

words.title: Jobs, skills and compound nouns

items.def: A person who helps people move properly again after an injury.
items.example: The physiotherapist showed my brother some exercises for his knee.
items.example_vi: Chuyên viên vật lý trị liệu chỉ cho anh trai tôi vài bài tập cho đầu gối.

items.def: A doctor for animals.
items.example: We took our cat to the vet when she stopped eating.
items.example_vi: Chúng tôi đưa mèo đi khám thú y khi nó bỏ ăn.

items.def: A person whose job is writing the code that makes computers work.
items.example: My aunt is a computer programmer and she writes code all day.
items.example_vi: Dì tôi là lập trình viên máy tính và cả ngày dì viết mã.

items.def: A person who designs, builds or repairs machines, roads or bridges.
items.example: I'm really good at fixing things, so I'd like to be an engineer.
items.example_vi: Em rất giỏi sửa đồ nên em muốn làm kỹ sư.

items.def: A film that shows real animals and plants in nature.
items.example: We watched a wildlife documentary about penguins last night.
items.example_vi: Tối qua chúng tôi xem một phim tài liệu về động vật hoang dã nói về chim cánh cụt.

items.def: Damage to your body that happens while you are playing sport.
items.example: A physiotherapist can help you get better after a sports injury.
items.example_vi: Chuyên viên vật lý trị liệu có thể giúp bạn hồi phục sau chấn thương thể thao.

items.def: Time spent working in a real job so that you learn what it is like.
items.example: She did two weeks of work experience at an animal hospital.
items.example_vi: Chị ấy đi thực tế hai tuần ở một bệnh viện thú y.

items.def: Work that you do to help other people, without being paid.
items.example: Voluntary work at the park helped him get his first job.
items.example_vi: Công việc tình nguyện ở công viên giúp anh ấy có việc làm đầu tiên.

words.note: Work experience, voluntary work and a university degree are three things that can help you get a job.

readings.title: People describing how they got their jobs
readings.about: Several speakers say what they were good at or keen on when they were young, and how those interests led to the job they do now.

summary.big_en: A work uniform is designed feature by feature, and every feature has a reason behind it: the weather, safety, carrying things, or comfort.

words.title: Uniform design

items.def: Showing up in the dark when light shines on it.
items.example: The white stripe is reflective, so drivers can see you at night.
items.example_vi: Sọc trắng có phản quang nên người lái xe nhìn thấy bạn vào ban đêm.

items.def: An important part of something.
items.example: The best feature of the jacket is its inside pockets.
items.example_vi: Điểm hay nhất của chiếc áo khoác là các túi bên trong.

items.def: To be right for a person, a purpose or a situation.
items.example: The loose design will suit people who are all shapes and sizes.
items.example_vi: Kiểu dáng rộng rãi này hợp với mọi vóc dáng và kích cỡ.

items.def: A long narrow band of colour.
items.example: The tracksuit is dark blue with a green stripe along the sleeves.
items.example_vi: Bộ đồ thể thao màu xanh đậm với một sọc xanh lá chạy dọc tay áo.

items.def: A fastener with two rows of teeth that lock together.
items.example: The trousers have zips at the bottom and zipped pockets on the side.
items.example_vi: Chiếc quần có khoá kéo ở gấu và túi có khoá ở hai bên.

items.def: Not letting water through.
items.example: Waterproof material from the ankle to the knee keeps the trousers dry.
items.example_vi: Lớp vải chống nước từ mắt cá đến đầu gối giữ cho ống quần luôn khô.

items.def: A small design that shows which company something belongs to.
items.example: The jacket has the post office logo at the top on the front right.
items.example_vi: Áo khoác có logo bưu điện ở phía trên bên phải mặt trước.

items.def: Able to get longer or wider and then go back to its shape.
items.example: The fabric is stretchy, so the uniform is comfortable to work in.
items.example_vi: Vải co giãn nên bộ đồng phục mặc làm việc rất thoải mái.

words.note: A good uniform answers four questions: is it right for the weather, is it safe, can you carry your things, and is it comfortable?

readings.title: Seb's design for a work uniform
readings.about: Seb describes a tracksuit-style uniform for a postman or postwoman, feature by feature, and gives a reason for every feature he chose.

summary.big_en: An astronaut's job is risky, exciting and hard work. Reported speech is how you pass on what somebody told you about their job.

grammar.title: Reported speech
grammar.when: Use reported speech to tell somebody what another person said, without using their exact words.
grammar.form: say / tell + (that) + clause

examples.en: Karina says that she has done three spacewalks so far.
examples.why: her words were 'I have done three spacewalks so far'

examples.en: She doesn't say that she has done one spacewalk.
examples.why: negative: doesn't say that…

examples.en: She explains that research in space today will help space travel in the future.
examples.why: explain works like say

examples.en: My uncle told me that he loved his job.
examples.why: tell needs a person after it

grammar.watch: Say goes straight to that (She said that…); tell needs a person first (She told me that…).

words.title: Space work and personal qualities

items.def: A trip outside a spacecraft while it is in space.
items.example: Karina has done three spacewalks so far.
items.example_vi: Đến giờ Karina đã thực hiện ba lần đi bộ ngoài không gian.

items.def: The force that pulls things down towards a planet.
items.example: There is almost no gravity on the space station, so everything floats.
items.example_vi: Trên trạm vũ trụ gần như không có trọng lực nên mọi thứ đều lơ lửng.

items.def: Travelling to a new place to find out what is there.
items.example: She has always been interested in space exploration and science.
items.example_vi: Cô ấy luôn hứng thú với việc khám phá vũ trụ và khoa học.

items.def: A little dangerous.
items.example: Working outside the space station is risky, so astronauts train for years.
items.example_vi: Làm việc bên ngoài trạm vũ trụ khá nguy hiểm nên phi hành gia phải luyện tập nhiều năm.

items.def: Sure that you can do something well.
items.example: You have to be confident to speak in front of the whole school.
items.example_vi: Bạn phải tự tin mới nói được trước toàn trường.

items.def: Showing that you enjoy something very much.
items.example: She is enthusiastic about her job and talks about it all the time.
items.example_vi: Cô ấy rất hào hứng với công việc và lúc nào cũng nói về nó.

items.def: Ready to try new and exciting things.
items.example: Astronauts are adventurous people who like new challenges.
items.example_vi: Phi hành gia là những người thích phiêu lưu và ưa thử thách mới.

items.def: Putting a lot of effort into your work or study.
items.example: You need to be hardworking to train as an astronaut.
items.example_vi: Bạn phải chăm chỉ mới theo được khoá huấn luyện phi hành gia.

words.note: Some opposites are made with the prefix un-: fit → unfit, adventurous → unadventurous, enthusiastic → unenthusiastic. Others are a different word: confident → shy, hardworking → lazy, exciting → boring.

readings.title: Interview with Karina, an American astronaut
readings.about: Karina talks about experiments in space, spacewalks, and how research today will help space travel in the future. In the second part she names the qualities an astronaut needs.

summary.big_en: A job advert says who you are looking for, what skills the candidate needs and where the interview is. It uses the present continuous and short sentences with no pronoun.

grammar.title: Present continuous review
grammar.when: Use the present continuous for something that is happening now and that we think is temporary.
grammar.form: am / is / are + verb-ing

examples.en: We are looking for a friendly zookeeper.
examples.why: the search will not last for ever

examples.en: We are recruiting genius-level inventors to form a new team.
examples.why: temporary situation, happening at the moment

examples.en: We are interviewing now. Call us on 6976 5454.
examples.why: happening around the time of the advert

grammar.watch: The subject and be must agree: we are looking, not 'we is looking'.

grammar.title: Shortened sentences in job adverts
grammar.when: Adverts save space by cutting out words that the reader can guess, especially the pronoun you.
grammar.form: (You) must be + adjective / (Experience is) needed

examples.en: Must be able to do experiments.
examples.why: the full sentence is 'You must be able to do experiments'

examples.en: Experience needed.
examples.why: the full sentence is 'Experience is needed'

examples.en: Must be good with heights.
examples.why: no pronoun, straight to must

grammar.watch: Only adverts and notices are written like this. In a normal sentence you must keep the pronoun.

items.def: A person who looks after the animals in a zoo.
items.example: We are looking for a friendly zookeeper to lead our team of animal carers.
items.example_vi: Chúng tôi đang tìm một người trông thú thân thiện để dẫn dắt nhóm chăm sóc động vật.

items.def: A performer who does jumps and balances, often high in the air.
items.example: An acrobat must be able to balance on one leg.
items.example_vi: Diễn viên nhào lộn phải đứng thăng bằng được trên một chân.

items.def: A person who is trying to get a job.
items.example: Which candidate is the most suitable for this job?
items.example_vi: Ứng viên nào phù hợp nhất với công việc này?

items.def: Able to bend and move your body easily.
items.example: You must be very flexible, strong and athletic to join our troupe.
items.example_vi: Bạn phải rất dẻo dai, khoẻ và có thể lực tốt mới vào được đoàn của chúng tôi.

items.def: Strong, fit and good at sport.
items.example: Acrobats are athletic and they train every day.
items.example_vi: Diễn viên nhào lộn có thể lực tốt và họ tập luyện mỗi ngày.

items.def: Difficult, but in a way that is interesting.
items.example: This job is more challenging than it looks!
items.example_vi: Công việc này khó hơn vẻ ngoài của nó nhiều!

lines: We are looking for an enthusiastic acrobat to join our troupe.
We are looking for a friendly zookeeper to lead our team of animal carers.
Could you invent the world's next best-selling gadget?
Must be very flexible, strong and athletic.
Must be interested in ALL kinds of animals.
Must be fascinated by science.
Experience needed.
Interviews will be held on the tightrope.
For further details, please visit our website.

readings.title: Three job adverts: acrobat, zookeeper and inventor
readings.about: Each advert opens by saying who the team is looking for, lists the skills the candidate must have, and ends with a surprising interview place.

summary.big_en: The poem 'You can be anything' says any job is possible if you try. It is built on could + be, on job words ending in -er, -or and -ist, and on rhyming vowel sounds.

grammar.title: could + be
grammar.when: Use could + be to say that something is possible in the future. It is not a promise and it is not permission.
grammar.form: subject + could + be + noun

examples.en: You could be a doctor and look after the sick.
examples.why: it is possible that you will be a doctor

examples.en: You could be a dentist and fix a cracked tooth.
examples.why: one of many possible futures

examples.en: You could be a police officer patrolling the roads.
examples.why: same pattern, followed by an -ing phrase

grammar.watch: Could is not the past of can here: it talks about a possible future, so 'You could be a scientist' means it may happen, not that it will.

words.title: Job words with the suffixes -er, -or and -ist

items.def: A person whose job is building houses and other buildings.
items.example: You could be a builder building houses, brick after brick.
items.example_vi: Bạn có thể làm thợ xây, xây nhà từng viên gạch một.

items.def: A person whose job is making walls and ceilings smooth.
items.example: A plasterer smooths the walls in bedrooms, kitchens and halls.
items.example_vi: Thợ trát làm phẳng những bức tường trong phòng ngủ, bếp và sảnh.

items.def: A person who cuts and styles people's hair.
items.example: You could be a hairdresser and cut people's hair.
items.example_vi: Bạn có thể làm thợ làm tóc và cắt tóc cho mọi người.

items.def: A person who performs in plays or films.
items.example: You could be an actor and dress up all day.
items.example_vi: Bạn có thể làm diễn viên và hoá trang cả ngày.

items.def: A doctor who looks after people's teeth.
items.example: The dentist fixed my cracked tooth in ten minutes.
items.example_vi: Nha sĩ chữa chiếc răng bị nứt của tôi chỉ trong mười phút.

items.def: A person who studies science or does research.
items.example: A scientist is finding new medicines that help mend the ill.
items.example_vi: Một nhà khoa học đang tìm ra những loại thuốc mới giúp chữa lành người bệnh.

items.def: Bumpy and uneven, not straight or flat.
items.example: The plasterer smoothed the wonky wall until it was flat.
items.example_vi: Người thợ trát làm phẳng bức tường gồ ghề cho đến khi nhẵn mịn.

words.note: The suffix turns a word into the person who does it: build → builder, act → actor, science → scientist. Watch out for police officer and firefighter, which are compound nouns instead.

sounds.title: Rhyming vowel sounds at the end of a line
sounds.focus: In each verse of the poem, the last words of two lines share the same vowel sound. Listen to the vowel, not the spelling: day and may rhyme, and so do hair and dare even though the letters are different.
sounds.note: Four different vowel sounds appear at the ends of lines in this poem: /eɪ/ (day, way), /er/ (hair, share), /aɪ/ (try, my) and /ɔː/ (walls, falls).

readings.title: You can be anything, by Teri Hopkins
readings.about: The poem names many very different jobs, from doctor to plasterer, and repeats one message: never give up, and the only person who chooses your job is you.

summary.big_en: A volcano can throw out lava, ash and gas without warning. To tell the story you need the past continuous for the long action and the past simple for the sudden one.

grammar.title: Past continuous
grammar.when: Use the past continuous for a longer action that was already happening when something shorter and sudden interrupted it, or for two actions happening at the same time.
grammar.form: was / were + verb-ing
