examples.en: We were making a film in Indonesia when the volcano suddenly exploded.
examples.why: the filming was already going on; the explosion cut into it

examples.en: We were almost a kilometre away when the lava was rolling towards us.
examples.why: the lava kept moving for a long time

examples.en: Houses were disappearing as the earth opened up in huge cracks.
examples.why: two things happening together

examples.en: We were in the area near the volcano while it was erupting.
examples.why: while joins two long actions

grammar.watch: The short, sudden event stays in the past simple (exploded); only the longer background action takes the past continuous.

items.def: Hot melted rock that flows out of a volcano.
items.example: We were almost a kilometre away when the lava was rolling towards us.
items.example_vi: Chúng tôi ở cách gần một ki-lô-mét khi dòng dung nham đang trôi về phía mình.

items.def: To throw out lava, ash and gas suddenly.
items.example: The volcano erupted while we were filming nearby.
items.example_vi: Ngọn núi lửa phun trào khi chúng tôi đang quay phim gần đó.

items.def: To burst apart suddenly with a loud noise.
items.example: The volcano suddenly exploded and we ran back to the car.
items.example_vi: Núi lửa bất ngờ nổ tung và chúng tôi chạy về phía xe.

items.def: The large round hole in the top of a volcano.
items.example: Smoke was rising from the crater at the top of the mountain.
items.example_vi: Khói đang bốc lên từ miệng núi lửa trên đỉnh.

items.def: The soft grey powder that is left after something burns.
items.example: A volcanic eruption can throw ash high into the air.
items.example_vi: Một đợt phun trào núi lửa có thể hất tro bụi lên cao trong không khí.

items.def: A long thin line where something has split open.
items.example: Houses were disappearing as the earth opened up in huge cracks.
items.example_vi: Những ngôi nhà biến mất khi mặt đất nứt toác thành những khe lớn.

items.def: A very large sea wave caused by an earthquake or an eruption.
items.example: If volcanoes erupt near water, they can cause a tsunami.
items.example_vi: Nếu núi lửa phun trào gần nước, chúng có thể gây ra sóng thần.

readings.title: A photographer talks about filming volcanoes
readings.about: In Part 1 he describes being close to a volcano while it was erupting. In Part 2 he says what you can see, hear, feel and smell there, and what good things volcanoes have done for the Earth.

summary.big_en: Lightning is electricity made inside a storm cloud when pieces of ice bump into each other. Positive and negative charges pull together, and the spark jumps.

words.title: Storms, electricity and physical change

items.def: To make something exist, or to take shape.
items.example: The tiny drops of water cool and form thunder clouds.
items.example_vi: Những giọt nước li ti nguội đi và tạo thành mây dông.

items.def: A measure of the amount of heat in something.
items.example: At the top of the cloud the temperature is very cold.
items.example_vi: Ở đỉnh đám mây, nhiệt độ rất lạnh.

items.def: The amount of electricity that something has.
items.example: The tiny ice crystals have a positive charge.
items.example_vi: Những tinh thể băng li ti mang điện tích dương.

items.def: To knock against something by accident.
items.example: The storm winds make the pieces of ice bump into each other.
items.example_vi: Gió bão làm các mảnh băng va vào nhau.

items.def: To hit something suddenly and hard.
items.example: Lightning often strikes trees, towers and sometimes even people.
items.example_vi: Sét thường đánh vào cây, tháp và đôi khi cả con người.

items.def: Having a lot of water in the air.
items.example: Warm ground makes warm, humid air which rises to the sky.
items.example_vi: Mặt đất ấm tạo ra luồng không khí ấm và ẩm bốc lên trời.

items.def: A very small flash of fire or electricity.
items.example: A huge spark of lightning happens inside the cloud.
items.example_vi: Một tia lửa điện khổng lồ loé lên bên trong đám mây.

items.def: To stay somewhere safe, away from danger or bad weather.
items.example: If you can't shelter in a building, shelter in a car.
items.example_vi: Nếu không trú được trong nhà, hãy trú trong ô tô.

words.note: Positive and negative are the two kinds of charge: opposite charges pull towards each other, and that is what makes lightning strike.

readings.title: How does lightning happen?
readings.about: The text follows warm humid air up into a storm cloud, explains how bumping pieces of ice make an electric charge, and ends with lightning travelling between the cloud and the ground.

summary.big_en: Earthquakes happen when stuck tectonic plates break free along a fault line. Safety advice is short: imperative verbs joined with until, as soon as and while.

grammar.title: Connecting words: until, as soon as, while
grammar.when: Use these words to show when something happens in relation to something else.
grammar.form: until = up to a point in time · as soon as = immediately after · while = at the same time as

examples.en: As soon as the shaking starts, get down on your hands and knees.
examples.why: do it immediately after the shaking begins

examples.en: Stay inside until the shaking stops.
examples.why: stay from now up to that moment

examples.en: Don't move from where you are while the earthquake is happening.
examples.why: during the whole time it lasts

examples.en: Hold on to the table legs until the shaking stops.
examples.why: keep holding right up to that point

grammar.watch: Until says when something ends; while says how long two things go on together. Swapping them changes the advice completely.

words.title: Verbs of movement and earthquake words

items.def: To lower your body towards the ground.
items.example: As soon as the shaking starts, get down on your hands and knees.
items.example_vi: Ngay khi mặt đất rung, hãy hạ người xuống bằng hai tay và hai đầu gối.

items.def: To put something over another thing to protect it.
items.example: Cover your head with your arms when the shaking starts.
items.example_vi: Hãy lấy tay che đầu khi mặt đất bắt đầu rung.

items.def: To move along on your hands and knees.
items.example: Crawl under a strong table and stay there.
items.example_vi: Hãy bò xuống dưới một chiếc bàn chắc chắn và ở yên đó.

items.def: To keep tight hold of something.
items.example: Hold on to the table legs until the shaking stops.
items.example_vi: Hãy bám chặt chân bàn cho đến khi hết rung lắc.

items.def: To move quickly from side to side or up and down.
items.example: The whole building shook for about twenty seconds.
items.example_vi: Cả toà nhà rung lắc khoảng hai mươi giây.

items.def: A break in the Earth's surface.
items.example: Earthquakes happen in places where there is a fault line.
items.example_vi: Động đất xảy ra ở những nơi có đường đứt gãy.

items.def: The huge blocks of moving rock under the Earth's surface.
items.example: When the tectonic plates break free, the pressure is released.
items.example_vi: Khi các mảng kiến tạo bung ra, áp lực được giải phóng.

items.def: The force that something makes when it pushes.
items.example: If the rocks get stuck, a lot of pressure builds up.
items.example_vi: Nếu các khối đá bị kẹt, áp lực rất lớn sẽ dồn lại.

groups.when: As soon as the shaking starts
lines: Get down on your hands and knees.
Cover your head with your arms.
Crawl under a strong table.
Hold on to the table legs until the shaking stops.
Stay inside.
Don't move from where you are.

readings.title: How do earthquakes happen?
readings.about: Tectonic plates usually slide past each other along a fault line. If they get stuck, pressure builds up, and when they break free the rock breaks and an earthquake happens.

readings.title: Earthquake public service broadcast
readings.about: A short radio announcement tells people what to do during an earthquake, using imperative verbs and connecting words so the advice is easy to remember.

summary.big_en: A good description of a place starts with a surprising fact and ends with feelings. Feelings need the right preposition: amazed by, interested in, sad about.

grammar.title: Adjectives + prepositions for feelings
grammar.when: Use a preposition after these adjectives to say how a place or an event made you feel.
grammar.form: be / feel + adjective + preposition + noun

examples.en: I was really amazed by what I saw.
examples.why: amazed always takes by

examples.en: I was fascinated by the stone figures of the people.
examples.why: fascinated also takes by

examples.en: I was really interested in the history and how the people lived.
examples.why: interested takes in

examples.en: I felt very sad about them at the same time.
examples.why: sad takes about

grammar.watch: Each adjective keeps its own preposition, so learn them in pairs: amazed by, fascinated by, interested in, sad about.

words.title: Describing a place and what happened there

items.def: Able to make you very ill, or to kill you.
items.example: The cloud was a poisonous mixture of ash and gas.
items.example_vi: Đám mây là một hỗn hợp độc hại gồm tro và khí.

items.def: Two or more different things put together.
items.example: Concrete is a mixture of sand, stone and water.
items.example_vi: Bê tông là hỗn hợp của cát, đá và nước.

items.def: To damage something so badly that it no longer exists.
items.example: The ash cloud destroyed houses and killed thousands of people.
items.example_vi: Đám mây tro đã phá huỷ nhà cửa và cướp đi sinh mạng hàng nghìn người.

items.def: Very old, from a time long ago.
items.example: My history project is about the ancient Romans.
items.example_vi: Bài tập lịch sử của em nói về người La Mã cổ đại.

items.def: Tools that you use for cooking and eating.
items.example: You can still see bread, bottles and cooking utensils in the old city.
items.example_vi: Bạn vẫn có thể thấy bánh mì, chai lọ và dụng cụ nấu ăn trong thành phố cổ.

items.def: A line of things or people next to each other.
items.example: You can see rows of houses and shops just as they were long ago.
items.example_vi: Bạn có thể nhìn thấy những dãy nhà và cửa hàng y như thuở xưa.

items.def: A strong feeling such as joy, fear or sadness.
items.example: My visit to Pompeii made me feel so many different emotions.
items.example_vi: Chuyến thăm Pompeii khiến em trải qua rất nhiều cảm xúc khác nhau.

readings.title: A special place: Hannah's visit to Pompeii
readings.about: Hannah opens with surprising facts about the eruption of CE79, then describes the streets, people and everyday objects she saw, and ends with how the visit made her feel.

summary.big_en: 'Thank You Letter' is a poem that thanks the sun for dawns, sunsets and ripening fruit, and it works by putting matching sounds next to each other.

words.title: Words for the sun and the sky

items.def: The time when the sun rises in the morning.
items.example: We got up at dawn to watch the sun come up over the sea.
items.example_vi: Chúng tôi dậy lúc bình minh để ngắm mặt trời lên trên biển.

items.def: The time in the evening when the sun goes down.
items.example: Sunsets are the loveliest things I know.
items.example_vi: Hoàng hôn là điều đáng yêu nhất mà tôi biết.

items.def: A soft steady light.
items.example: In the evening the sky keeps the warm glow of the sun.
items.example_vi: Buổi tối bầu trời vẫn giữ lại ánh sáng ấm áp của mặt trời.

items.def: Very hot and bright.
items.example: Thanks for those blazing days on beaches.
items.example_vi: Cảm ơn vì những ngày nắng chói chang trên bãi biển.

items.def: Making fruit ready to eat.
items.example: Thank you for ripening apples, pears and peaches.
items.example_vi: Cảm ơn vì đã làm chín táo, lê và đào.

items.def: Grey and cold.
items.example: On dismal days the sun waits calmly behind the cloud.
items.example_vi: Vào những ngày xám lạnh, mặt trời điềm tĩnh chờ sau đám mây.

items.def: Strong and brave.
items.example: The sun shares out its noble glow with the whole world.
items.example_vi: Mặt trời chia sẻ thứ ánh sáng mạnh mẽ của mình với cả thế giới.

sounds.title: Matching sounds
sounds.focus: Poets put words with the same sound close together. Listen for which part matches: sometimes it is the first consonant, as in warm and wonderful, and sometimes it is the vowel inside the word, as in bright and shining.
sounds.note: In 'Thanks for those / Blazing days on beaches' the /z/ sound repeats in those, blazing and days, and the /b/ sound repeats in blazing and beaches.

readings.title: Thank You Letter, by Eric Finney
readings.about: The poem is written as a letter to the sun. The writer thanks it for dawns and sunsets, for waiting behind the cloud on grey days, and for ripening fruit.

summary.big_en: We talk about what we watch and play at home using the words for the parts of a film or game, and participle adjectives to say how it all feels.

grammar.title: Participle adjectives
grammar.when: Use an -ed adjective for how a person feels, and an -ing adjective for the thing that causes the feeling.
grammar.form: verb + -ed (the feeling) / verb + -ing (what causes it)

examples.en: My mum was a bit worried.
examples.why: -ed: this is how she felt

examples.en: The graphics are amazing!
examples.why: -ing: the graphics cause the feeling

examples.en: There's no time to get bored!
examples.why: -ed: how the player feels

examples.en: It's quite difficult to play and that makes it more exciting.
examples.why: -ing: the game causes the excitement

grammar.watch: 'I am boring' means you make other people bored; say 'I am bored' for how you feel (p.129).

words.title: Film and video game features

items.def: The story of a film, book or game: what happens and in what order.
items.example: The plot is really exciting because you never know who the hero can trust.
items.example_vi: Cốt truyện rất hấp dẫn vì bạn không bao giờ biết người hùng có thể tin ai.

items.def: Drawings or computer images that are made to move.
items.example: The animation in this cartoon is so smooth that the animals look real.
items.example_vi: Phần hoạt hình trong phim này mượt đến mức các con vật trông như thật.

items.def: All the music used in a film or a game.
items.example: The soundtrack is awesome, so I listen to it while I do my homework.
items.example_vi: Nhạc phim hay tuyệt, nên tớ mở nghe trong lúc làm bài tập.

items.def: The pictures a computer or a game makes on the screen.
items.example: The graphics are amazing on the new game.
items.example_vi: Đồ hoạ của trò chơi mới đẹp đến kinh ngạc.

items.def: Tricks that show on screen things a camera cannot really film.
items.example: The special effects brought life-like dinosaurs to the screen.
items.example_vi: Kỹ xảo đã đưa những con khủng long y như thật lên màn ảnh.

items.def: All the actors who appear in a film or a play.
items.example: The cast of this film is small: only four actors ever speak.
items.example_vi: Dàn diễn viên của phim rất ít: chỉ có bốn người có thoại.

items.def: The clothes an actor wears to play a character.
items.example: The actors wore space costumes made of silver cloth.
items.example_vi: Các diễn viên mặc trang phục phi hành gia bằng vải bạc.

items.def: The place and the time where a story happens.
items.example: The setting of the story is an island theme park full of dinosaurs.
items.example_vi: Bối cảnh của câu chuyện là một công viên trên đảo đầy khủng long.

words.note: Activity 3 asks which of these features belong to films, to board games and to video games.

readings.title: Rory talks about his video game
readings.about: Rory names the features of the game he plays at home and gives three good points about it. His mum was worried about the game, so he explains that you have to know when to stop.

summary.big_en: Films grew from a one-person peephole machine in 1891 into colour movies in 1935, and that history is told with the past simple passive.

grammar.title: Past simple passive
grammar.when: Use it for past events when you want to focus on the event itself, not on the person who did it.
grammar.form: was / were + past participle (+ by + the doer)

examples.en: These early films were made in black and white.
examples.why: the films matter, not the film makers

examples.en: In 1891, the first film projector was invented by the Edison company.
examples.why: by names the doer

examples.en: The first moving pictures were shown to an audience in 1895.
examples.why: plural subject, so were

examples.en: Popcorn was sold in cinemas for the first time in 1912.
examples.why: singular subject, so was

grammar.watch: Use was for one thing and were for more than one, then always the past participle (p.131).

words.title: Films in the past

items.def: A machine that shows moving pictures on a screen.
items.example: The first film projector showed moving pictures on a tiny screen inside the machine.
items.example_vi: Chiếc máy chiếu phim đầu tiên chiếu hình ảnh chuyển động trên một màn hình nhỏ xíu bên trong máy.

items.def: A film with no recorded sound.
items.example: From 1907, people watched silent films in cinemas on big screens.
items.example_vi: Từ năm 1907, người ta xem phim câm trên màn ảnh lớn trong rạp.

items.def: The first films that had sound and dialogue.
items.example: Films with sound appeared in 1927 and people called them talkies.
items.example_vi: Phim có tiếng xuất hiện năm 1927 và người ta gọi chúng là phim nói.

items.def: The look on someone's face that shows what they feel.
items.example: Silent film actors used their facial expressions to show what was happening.
items.example_vi: Diễn viên phim câm dùng nét mặt để cho thấy chuyện gì đang xảy ra.

items.def: A person who plays the piano.
items.example: The only sound in the cinema came from a pianist near the screen.
items.example_vi: Âm thanh duy nhất trong rạp phát ra từ một người chơi dương cầm cạnh màn ảnh.

words.note: The five years on the timeline are 1895, 1907, 1912, 1927 and 1935.

readings.title: How films began
readings.about: A movie expert follows films from the 1891 peephole projector to the first paying audience in 1895 and silent films from 1907. Sound arrived in 1927 and colour in 1935.

summary.big_en: Too much screen time has real costs, so families agree a screen-time schedule and discuss it using adverbs of time and frequency.

grammar.title: Adverbs of time and frequency
grammar.when: These adverbs say when an action happens. Some give a definite (exact) time; others only say how often, without an exact time.
grammar.form: definite: today, tonight, daily, weekly · indefinite: often, usually, normally, sometimes

examples.en: We've talked today about what you do on your devices.
examples.why: today gives an exact time

examples.en: You have a limit of one hour of screen time daily.
examples.why: daily is exact: every day

examples.en: I often use my tablet for schoolwork.
examples.why: often does not say when

examples.en: What do you normally play or watch on a screen at the weekend?
examples.why: normally is how often, not when

grammar.watch: Adverbs of frequency usually go before the main verb: I sometimes use a device for homework (p.133).

words.title: Screen time

items.def: A plan that says when things happen.
items.example: Our screen-time schedule gives each of us one hour a day.
items.example_vi: Lịch dùng màn hình của nhà tớ cho mỗi người một tiếng mỗi ngày.

items.def: Not able to stop doing something.
items.example: Too much screen time can make you addicted to your device.
items.example_vi: Dùng màn hình quá nhiều có thể khiến bạn nghiện thiết bị.

items.def: Friendly and happy to be with other people.
items.example: Screens can stop you being sociable with the people around you.
items.example_vi: Màn hình có thể khiến bạn ít giao tiếp với những người xung quanh.

items.def: Easily made angry.
items.example: If I don't sleep properly, I'm bad-tempered all morning.
items.example_vi: Nếu ngủ không ngon, tớ cáu bẳn suốt cả buổi sáng.

items.def: To stop someone paying attention to something.
items.example: Games on my phone distract me from my school work.
items.example_vi: Mấy trò chơi trong điện thoại làm tớ xao nhãng việc học.

items.def: The most that is allowed.
items.example: You have a limit of one hour of screen time on a school day.
items.example_vi: Em có giới hạn một tiếng dùng màn hình vào ngày đi học.

words.note: The advert says many children spend 50+ hours a week in front of a screen.

I've got one more point to make. How about…?
I think that's a good idea.
Me too.
Yes, that sounds right.
Great idea!
No, I think it's better to…

readings.title: Hard truths about screen time!
readings.about: An advert for the TechTime app lists what too much screen time does to you, from bad sleep to being addicted to your device. It then suggests tech-free activities, no-tech zones and screen-time schedules.

readings.title: Mr Stern's class plan a screen-time schedule
readings.about: Lola, Kurran and Ali work out how many hours of screen time they can have in a week and how weekdays differ from weekends. They also decide what happens if someone uses more on one day.

summary.big_en: A storyboard turns a story into scenes, and direct speech with strong reporting verbs makes those scenes come alive.

grammar.title: Direct speech with reporting verbs
grammar.when: Use direct speech to make a story more interesting, and replace 'said' with a verb that shows how the words were spoken.
grammar.form: 'Spoken words,' + reporting verb + speaker (or ! instead of the comma)

examples.en: 'Here, let me make it more comfortable for you,' he sniggered.
examples.why: comma inside the speech marks, before the verb

examples.en: 'Oh, no, not again!' sighed Dad.
examples.why: an exclamation mark takes the place of the comma

examples.en: 'I know what will help!' said Dad.
examples.why: the speech marks hold only the spoken words

examples.en: 'No, Boris, I insist! You must sleep there,' insisted Horis.
examples.why: insisted shows he would not give in

grammar.watch: Reporting verbs to reuse: sighed, sniggered, whispered, insisted, promised, laughed (p.135).

items.def: To breathe out slowly to show you are sad or tired.
items.example: 'Oh no, not again!' sighed Dad.
items.example_vi: 'Ôi không, lại nữa rồi!' bố thở dài.

items.def: To laugh quietly in an unkind way.
items.example: 'Here's a good place for a tent… hee hee!' sniggered Boris.
items.example_vi: 'Đây là chỗ dựng lều tốt đấy… hi hi!' Boris cười khẩy.

items.def: To say something very firmly when someone disagrees.
items.example: 'No, Boris, I insist! You must sleep there,' said Horis.
items.example_vi: 'Không, Boris, tớ nhất định đấy! Cậu phải ngủ ở đó,' Horis nói.

items.def: To speak very quietly.
items.example: 'Look at that ants' nest,' whispered Horis.
items.example_vi: 'Nhìn cái tổ kiến kia kìa,' Horis thì thầm.

items.def: To say that you will certainly do something.
items.example: 'You'll love camping! Just think of all the fun we'll have,' promised Dad.
items.example_vi: 'Con sẽ mê cắm trại cho mà xem! Cứ nghĩ tới bao nhiêu trò vui đi,' bố hứa.

items.def: One short part of a film or a play.
items.example: In Scene 2, Dad and the boys look for a place for the tent.
items.example_vi: Ở cảnh 2, bố và hai cậu con trai đi tìm chỗ dựng lều.

items.def: A row of drawings that plans the scenes of a film.
items.example: We made a storyboard with six scenes for our film.
items.example_vi: Chúng tớ vẽ một bảng phân cảnh gồm sáu cảnh cho bộ phim.

groups.when: Making a suggestion to your group
lines: Why don't we add… to Scene 1?
Let's put a… in Scene 2…

readings.title: Horis and Boris: a camping storyboard
readings.about: Dad promises the twins a weekend of camping fun, but Boris picks a sleeping place for Horis right beside an ants' nest. Horis works out the trick and hands the place back, until Dad takes it himself.

summary.big_en: Jurassic Park was the film that put life-like CGI dinosaurs on screen, and in the novel extract Tina meets a friendly 'lizard' that is not a lizard at all.

words.title: Words from the Jurassic Park extract

items.def: A place out of the sunlight.
items.example: Tina moved back from the water to the shade of the palm trees.
items.example_vi: Tina lùi khỏi mép nước, vào bóng râm của những cây cọ.

items.def: To come out of somewhere.
items.example: A lizard emerged from the mangrove roots and peered at her.
items.example_vi: Một con thằn lằn chui ra từ đám rễ đước và nhìn chằm chằm vào cô bé.

items.def: At the back; used about an animal's back legs.
items.example: The lizard stood on its hind legs, balancing on its thick tail.
items.example_vi: Con thằn lằn đứng trên hai chân sau, giữ thăng bằng bằng cái đuôi dày.

items.def: The inside part of your hand.
items.example: She could feel its little toes pinching the skin of her palm.
items.example_vi: Cô bé cảm thấy những ngón chân bé xíu của nó bấu vào da lòng bàn tay.

items.def: How heavy something is.
items.example: She felt the surprising weight of the animal pressing her arm down.
items.example_vi: Cô bé cảm nhận sức nặng bất ngờ của con vật đè tay mình xuống.

items.def: To move quickly using your hands and feet.
items.example: The lizard scrambled up her arm towards her face.
items.example_vi: Con thằn lằn trèo nhoay nhoáy lên cánh tay, về phía mặt cô bé.

items.def: Very tired.
items.example: Tina ran until she was exhausted and then threw herself down on the sand.
items.example_vi: Tina chạy đến kiệt sức rồi buông mình xuống cát.

items.def: To make the short high sound a small bird makes.
items.example: The lizard paused, cocked its head and chirped.
items.example_vi: Con thằn lằn dừng lại, nghiêng đầu và kêu chiêm chiếp.

words.note: Activity 7 asks you to guess these meanings from the words around them, not from a dictionary.

sounds.title: Hard and soft th
sounds.focus: Your tongue is in the same place for both sounds; the difference is your voice. Hard th is /θ/ with no voice, and soft th is /ð/ with the voice switched on. Put a hand on your throat: soft th buzzes.
sounds.note: Little grammar words such as the, then, this and they nearly always take the soft /ð/.

readings.title: Jurassic Park: an introduction to the film
readings.about: Jurassic Park is a science-fiction film from 1993, based on a novel by Michael Crichton, about scientists visiting an island park of real dinosaurs. It is famous because CGI brought life-like dinosaurs to the screen.

readings.title: Jurassic Park, by Michael Crichton
readings.about: On a beach in Costa Rica, Tina notices three-toed tracks in the sand and a small green creature comes out of the mangroves. It walks on its hind legs, chirps at her and then jumps onto her hand.

summary.big_en: Art in public places carries a message for everybody who walks past, and indefinite pronouns let us talk about those people and places without naming them.

grammar.title: Indefinite pronouns
grammar.when: Use an indefinite pronoun to talk about people or things without saying exactly who, what, where or how many.
grammar.form: some- / any- / no- / every- + -one, -body, -thing, -where

examples.en: We can make something beautiful out of an old wall.
examples.why: something: a thing you do not name

examples.en: The murals send positive messages to everybody.
examples.why: everybody: all the people

examples.en: Anyone who visits festivals in Mexico can see the paper flags.
examples.why: anyone: any person at all

examples.en: There isn't anywhere in my town where you can see street art.
examples.why: anywhere after a negative verb

grammar.watch: -one and -body are for people, -thing for things, -where for places. Nobody and nothing are already negative, so do not add 'not' as well (p.145).

words.title: Types of art and materials

items.def: A work of art shaped in three dimensions from stone, metal or other materials.
items.example: The fish sculpture is made from old materials, not new ones.
items.example_vi: Bức điêu khắc hình con cá được làm từ vật liệu cũ chứ không phải vật liệu mới.

items.def: A large picture painted on a wall.
items.example: The mural covers the metal wall with bright colours and a positive message.
items.example_vi: Bức tranh tường phủ lên bức vách kim loại những màu sắc rực rỡ và một thông điệp tích cực.

items.def: Cloth and other woven materials.
items.example: The 3D artwork is made of metal and textiles.
items.example_vi: Tác phẩm ba chiều này được làm bằng kim loại và vải dệt.

items.def: A picture made from many small coloured pieces stuck together.
items.example: The walls of the building are covered in coloured mosaics.
items.example_vi: Những bức tường của toà nhà được phủ bằng các mảnh khảm nhiều màu.

items.def: A strong, hard metal.
items.example: The red sculpture in the square is made of steel.
items.example_vi: Bức tượng đỏ ngoài quảng trường được làm bằng thép.

items.def: Paint that comes out of a can as a fine mist.
items.example: Street artists use spray paint to work quickly on a big wall.
items.example_vi: Các nghệ sĩ đường phố dùng sơn xịt để vẽ nhanh trên bức tường lớn.

items.def: A hard grey material used for building.
items.example: The wall of the underpass was grey concrete until the artists painted it.
items.example_vi: Bức tường của hầm đi bộ chỉ toàn bê tông xám cho tới khi các nghệ sĩ vẽ lên đó.

words.note: Activity 1 also names a paper flag pattern called lace and a decorative doorway.

readings.title: Five artworks and their messages
readings.about: Five public artworks are described: a fish sculpture built from recycled materials, a big blue doorway, a red sculpture about caring for each other, Mexican paper flags and a mural at the World Trade Centre site.

summary.big_en: In Cateura, Paraguay, a carpenter builds instruments out of landfill rubbish, and the present perfect shows how that work has changed lives right up to today.

grammar.title: Present perfect for unfinished past
grammar.when: Use it for something that started in the past and is still going on now. This is a different job from the present perfect for a finished event in the recent past.
grammar.form: have / has + past participle (+ for + a length of time, or since + a starting point)

examples.en: Ada Rios has played in the Orchestra for many years.
examples.why: she started years ago and still plays today

examples.en: The instruments have given hundreds of children the gift of music.
examples.why: it began in the past and is still happening

examples.en: Since then, Cola has used old metal tins to make violins.
examples.why: since marks a time that has not ended

examples.en: Since it started, the Recycled Orchestra has gone from strength to strength.
examples.why: the orchestra is still growing now

grammar.watch: Use for with a length of time (for many years) and since with a starting point (since then, since 2006) (p.147).

grammar.title: Concrete and abstract nouns
grammar.when: Sort a noun by asking whether you could meet it with your senses.
grammar.form: concrete = you can see, hear, touch, smell or taste it · abstract = an idea, a feeling or an emotion

examples.en: The orchestra plays violins, cellos, guitars and drums.
examples.why: concrete: you can see and hear them

examples.en: Music education helps children develop creativity and teamwork.
examples.why: abstract: skills and ideas

examples.en: The Recycled Orchestra is the pride of its community.
examples.why: abstract: a feeling

items.def: A large group of musicians who play together.
items.example: The Recycled Orchestra has performed concerts all over South America.
items.example_vi: Dàn nhạc Tái Chế đã biểu diễn khắp Nam Mỹ.

items.def: An instrument you play by pulling or rubbing the strings.
items.example: Cola makes violins, cellos and guitars, which are all string instruments.
items.example_vi: Chú Cola làm vi-ô-lông, xen-lô và ghi-ta, tất cả đều là nhạc cụ dây.

items.def: An instrument you play by blowing into it.
items.example: The saxophones and trumpets are wind instruments made from old pipes.
items.example_vi: Kèn saxophone và kèn trumpet là nhạc cụ hơi, làm từ những ống nước cũ.

items.def: Instruments you play by hitting them with your hand or a stick.
items.example: The drums are percussion, and these ones are made from metal tins.
items.example_vi: Trống thuộc bộ gõ, và những chiếc trống này được làm từ hộp thiếc.

items.def: A place where rubbish from a town is dumped or buried.
items.example: Cateura has mountains of landfill rubbish from the nearby capital city.
items.example_vi: Cateura có những núi rác thải đổ về từ thành phố thủ đô gần đó.

items.def: A person who makes things out of wood.
items.example: A local carpenter made the first violin out of bits of rubbish.
items.example_vi: Một bác thợ mộc trong vùng đã làm cây vi-ô-lông đầu tiên từ những mảnh rác.

readings.title: From trash to treasure: the Recycled Orchestra
readings.about: In Cateura, Paraguay, a music school had too few instruments, so a carpenter called Cola began building violins, drums and saxophones out of landfill rubbish. The orchestra is now the pride of its community and tours South America.

summary.big_en: Adverts for cultural events tell you what happens and exactly when, and present tenses are what carry that future meaning.

grammar.title: Present tenses with future meaning
grammar.when: Use the present simple for future events that are fixed by a timetable or a fact, and the present continuous for plans you have already arranged.
grammar.form: present simple = timetable · am / is / are + -ing = arrangement

examples.en: Their train leaves early on Wednesday morning.
examples.why: a timetable, so present simple

examples.en: They are arriving on Sunday and staying until Wednesday.
examples.why: a plan the family has already made

examples.en: The Virtual Experience starts at 4pm.
examples.why: a fixed schedule, even though it is still to come

examples.en: We're having lunch in the café at 1.45pm.
examples.why: an arrangement already decided

grammar.watch: The Star Circus tour opens on May 1st: a schedule keeps the present simple even months in advance (p.148).

items.def: The design and style of buildings.
items.example: Our city tour starts with the interesting architecture near the river.
items.example_vi: Chuyến tham quan thành phố bắt đầu với những công trình kiến trúc thú vị bên sông.

items.def: A model of a person or an animal made of stone or metal.
items.example: There is a statue of a horse in front of the museum.
items.example_vi: Có một bức tượng con ngựa ở trước bảo tàng.

items.def: Belonging to the present time; modern.
items.example: The park has a unique collection of contemporary sculpture.
items.example_vi: Công viên có một bộ sưu tập điêu khắc đương đại độc đáo.

items.def: A short class where you make or practise something.
items.example: The three-hour family workshop starts at 2pm.
items.example_vi: Buổi thực hành ba tiếng dành cho gia đình bắt đầu lúc 2 giờ chiều.

items.def: Difficult jumps and balances done by trained performers.
items.example: The circus opens with amazing acrobatics high above the stage.
items.example_vi: Rạp xiếc mở màn bằng những màn nhào lộn tuyệt vời trên cao.

items.def: A game in which you follow clues to find hidden things.
items.example: Download the city map and join our Art Safari treasure hunt.
items.example_vi: Hãy tải bản đồ thành phố và tham gia trò săn tìm kho báu Art Safari.

items.def: A plan of a journey that says where you go and when.
items.example: Our itinerary starts at the sculpture park and ends at the museum.
items.example_vi: Lịch trình của nhóm tớ bắt đầu ở công viên điêu khắc và kết thúc ở bảo tàng.

readings.title: Three adverts for cultural events
readings.about: An Art Safari treasure hunt runs from June to August, a sculpture park offers a three-hour family workshop that starts at 2pm, and the Star Circus tour opens on May 1st. Each advert includes an activity for visitors to do.

summary.big_en: A poem can let a building describe itself, using 'like' to compare it with something else and descriptive adjectives to paint the picture.

grammar.title: Uses of like
grammar.when: 'like' does two different jobs, so look at what comes after it.
grammar.form: verb: subject + like + noun or -ing · preposition: look / sound / feel + like + noun

examples.en: I like the shape of that building.
examples.why: verb: it says what you enjoy

examples.en: It looks like the sails on a ship.
examples.why: preposition: it compares two things

examples.en: I look like a magic house in a story book.
examples.why: preposition after look, in the poem

examples.en: The Gherkin reminds me of a vegetable, and it sounds like one too.
examples.why: preposition after sounds

grammar.watch: After 'looks like' you need a noun: It looks strange, but It looks like a shell (p.151).

items.def: Clean, bright and shiny.
items.example: I am made of smooth concrete and gleaming glass.
items.example_vi: Tôi được làm từ bê tông nhẵn mịn và kính sáng bóng.

items.def: Reflecting light in a soft, beautiful way.
items.example: I look out onto the shimmering ocean.
items.example_vi: Tôi nhìn ra mặt biển lấp lánh.

items.def: The deep blue colour of a precious stone.
items.example: I am made of coloured mosaics and sapphire glass.
items.example_vi: Tôi được làm từ những mảnh khảm màu và kính xanh lam.

items.def: Lit up so that it looks brighter.
items.example: The building is illuminated at night.
items.example_vi: Toà nhà được thắp sáng rực vào ban đêm.

items.def: Having a rounded shape.
items.example: I am bright, shiny and curved.
items.example_vi: Tôi sáng, bóng và uốn cong mềm mại.

items.def: With a line that goes up and down like waves.
items.example: I am wavy, strange and wonderful.
items.example_vi: Tôi uốn lượn, kỳ lạ và tuyệt vời.

items.def: Flat and even, with no rough parts.
items.example: The concrete walls feel smooth under your hand.
items.example_vi: Những bức tường bê tông sờ vào thấy nhẵn mịn.

phrases.title: A writing frame for a building poem

lines: I look like the sails on a huge white ship
I look like a magic house in a story book
I am made of smooth concrete and gleaming glass
I am made of coloured mosaics and sapphire glass
I am bright, shiny and curved
I am wavy, strange and wonderful

groups.when: What is around you and inside you?
lines: I look out onto the shimmering ocean
I am filled with artists, actors and musicians
I am filled with memories
What am I?

readings.title: Curved wonder and Mosaic magic
readings.about: Two famous buildings describe themselves in the first person and end by asking 'What am I?'. One looks like the sails of a huge white ship, the other like a magic house from a story book.

summary.big_en: Willow keeps painting what she sees behind her closed eyes, and in the end her gift changes her strict art teacher.

grammar.title: Adjective order
grammar.when: When you use more than one adjective before a noun, put them in a fixed order.
grammar.form: number/quantity → opinion → size → physical quality → colour → material → noun

examples.en: There wasn't a single broken crayon in the bunch.
examples.why: number, then physical quality, then the noun

examples.en: A beautiful red sunset.
examples.why: opinion comes before colour

examples.en: A huge crashing waterfall.
examples.why: size comes before physical quality

examples.en: Sweet golden fruit.
examples.why: taste is a physical quality, so it comes before colour

grammar.watch: 'A red, beautiful sunset' sounds wrong to English ears because opinion must come before colour (p.155).

words.title: Words for feelings and reactions

items.def: To laugh in a quiet, nervous way.
items.example: A few students giggled when Willow showed her pink tree.
items.example_vi: Vài bạn cười khúc khích khi Willow đưa ra bức tranh cây màu hồng.

items.def: A very annoyed look on someone's face.
items.example: Miss Hawthorn glanced at the picture, then turned away with a scowl.
items.example_vi: Cô Hawthorn liếc nhìn bức tranh rồi quay đi với vẻ mặt cau có.

items.def: To shake a little because you are cold or afraid.
items.example: Willow shivered when her teacher looked at her.
items.example_vi: Willow rùng mình khi cô giáo nhìn mình.

items.def: To look at someone in an angry way.
items.example: Miss Hawthorn's icy blue eyes glared at Willow.
items.example_vi: Đôi mắt xanh lạnh lẽo của cô Hawthorn quắc lên nhìn Willow.

items.def: An expression that shows you are annoyed or confused.
items.example: 'Whoever heard of a pink tree?' Miss Hawthorn asked with a frown.
items.example_vi: 'Ai mà nghe nói tới cây màu hồng bao giờ?' cô Hawthorn cau mày hỏi.

items.def: To speak quietly so that people can hardly hear you.
items.example: 'Horrid little girl,' she muttered as Willow skipped off.
items.example_vi: 'Con bé đáng ghét,' cô lẩm bẩm khi Willow tung tăng chạy đi.

items.def: To draw in a free, relaxed way, without planning.
items.example: For the first time in her life, Miss Hawthorn doodled.
items.example_vi: Lần đầu tiên trong đời, cô Hawthorn vẽ nguệch ngoạc cho vui.

words.note: Activity 5 asks you to match these words to their meanings using the words around them in the story.

sounds.title: The two sounds of the letter i
sounds.focus: The same letter i gives two sounds. It is long /aɪ/ when the syllable is open or ends in a silent e, and short /ɪ/ when a consonant or a pair of consonants closes the syllable.
sounds.note: Adding -ed or -ing does not change the sound: skipped stays /ɪ/ and stinks stays /ɪ/.

readings.title: Willow, by Denise Brennan-Nelson and Rosemarie Brennan
readings.about: In Miss Hawthorn's cold, tidy art room, Willow paints a pink tree and then a blue apple, and gets into trouble every time. On the last day of term she gives the teacher her own well-loved art book, and that evening Miss Hawthorn doodles for the first time in her life.

flashcards.front_en: When do you use the present perfect?
flashcards.back_en: For recent events when the exact time does not matter. Form: have or has + past participle.

flashcards.front_en: How do you ask about someone's experience?
flashcards.back_en: Have you ever…? — for example, Have you ever felt really proud of yourself?

flashcards.front_en: Latitude or longitude: which runs pole to pole?
flashcards.back_en: Longitude. Latitude circles the Earth parallel to the equator.

flashcards.front_en: How far apart are the lines of latitude?
flashcards.back_en: About 111 km, and each distance is measured in degrees.

flashcards.front_en: Three sequencing phrases for a presentation?
flashcards.back_en: Today, I'm going to talk about… / As I said in my introduction… / To sum up…

flashcards.front_en: Noun forms of proud, amazing, exciting?
flashcards.back_en: pride, amazement, excitement.

flashcards.front_en: Give an example of verb + object + infinitive.
flashcards.back_en: My dad taught me to swim. / My friend asked me to go with him.
The things that make you who you are.
flashcards.example_en: Your name and your language are both part of your identity.
flashcards.example_vi: Tên và tiếng nói của em đều là một phần bản sắc của em.

flashcards.back_en: Lines that circle the Earth parallel to the equator.
flashcards.example_en: Lines of latitude are measured 0–90° to the north and to the south.
flashcards.example_vi: Vĩ tuyến được đo từ 0 đến 90 độ về phía bắc và phía nam.

flashcards.back_en: Lines that run from the North Pole to the South Pole.
flashcards.example_en: Lines of longitude divide the Earth's surface into vertical sections.
flashcards.example_vi: Kinh tuyến chia bề mặt Trái Đất thành những phần thẳng đứng.

flashcards.back_en: The imaginary line circling the Earth halfway between the poles.
flashcards.example_en: In the middle, circling the Earth between the two poles, is the equator.
flashcards.example_vi: Ở giữa, vòng quanh Trái Đất giữa hai cực, là đường xích đạo.

flashcards.back_en: The first part of a talk, where you say what it is about.
flashcards.example_en: As I said in my introduction, she is a young activist.
flashcards.example_vi: Như em đã nói ở phần mở đầu, cô ấy là một nhà hoạt động trẻ.

flashcards.back_en: Words and phrases that show your audience the order of your ideas.
flashcards.example_en: Sequencing words like 'to sum up' help your audience follow you.
flashcards.example_vi: Những từ nối như 'tóm lại' giúp người nghe theo được mạch bài.

flashcards.back_en: To come first in a game or competition.
flashcards.example_en: Our team won the match by two goals.
flashcards.example_vi: Đội của chúng tôi thắng trận với cách biệt hai bàn.

flashcards.back_en: To hurt or frighten someone weaker, again and again.
flashcards.example_en: Nobody should bully a younger child at school.
flashcards.example_vi: Không ai được bắt nạt em nhỏ hơn ở trường.

flashcards.back_en: Very good indeed.
flashcards.example_en: The view from the top of the mountain was awesome.
flashcards.example_vi: Khung cảnh từ đỉnh núi đẹp đến kinh ngạc.

flashcards.back_en: Unkind to other people.
flashcards.example_en: It was mean of him to laugh at her drawing.
flashcards.example_vi: Cậu ấy cười nhạo bức vẽ của bạn là rất ác ý.

flashcards.back_en: Damage or injury done to someone or something.
flashcards.example_en: Too much sun can harm your skin.
flashcards.example_vi: Nắng nhiều quá có thể làm hại da của bạn.

flashcards.back_en: To suffer or die because there is no food.
flashcards.example_en: Without rain the crops fail and people starve.
flashcards.example_vi: Không có mưa thì mùa màng mất trắng và người ta chết đói.

flashcards.back_en: The most northern or the most southern point of the Earth.
flashcards.example_en: At one end is the North Pole and at the other, the South Pole.
flashcards.example_vi: Một đầu là Bắc Cực, đầu kia là Nam Cực.

flashcards.back_en: A unit of measurement.
flashcards.example_en: The equator's line of latitude is zero degrees.
flashcards.example_vi: Đường vĩ tuyến của xích đạo là không độ.

flashcards.back_en: Two lines that stay the same distance apart.
flashcards.example_en: More lines of latitude circle the Earth parallel to the equator.
flashcards.example_vi: Các vĩ tuyến khác vòng quanh Trái Đất song song với xích đạo.

flashcards.back_en: Standing upwards.
flashcards.example_en: The lines divide the Earth's surface into vertical sections.
flashcards.example_vi: Các đường này chia bề mặt Trái Đất thành những phần thẳng đứng.

flashcards.back_en: A code that shows an exact position on a map.
flashcards.example_en: Bangkok is at the coordinate 13° N 100° E.
flashcards.example_vi: Bangkok nằm ở toạ độ 13° Bắc 100° Đông.

flashcards.back_en: A person who takes action to support their beliefs.
flashcards.example_en: Malala Yousafzai is an activist for girls' education.
flashcards.example_vi: Malala Yousafzai là nhà hoạt động vì quyền học tập của trẻ em gái.

flashcards.back_en: To think very well of someone.
flashcards.example_en: I admire her because she never gave up.
flashcards.example_vi: Em khâm phục cô ấy vì cô ấy không bao giờ bỏ cuộc.

flashcards.back_en: To refuse to allow something.
flashcards.example_en: They banned girls from going to school.
flashcards.example_vi: Họ cấm các bé gái đến trường.

flashcards.back_en: The internet, newspapers, TV and magazines.
flashcards.example_en: Her story appeared in the media all over the world.
flashcards.example_vi: Câu chuyện của cô ấy xuất hiện trên truyền thông khắp thế giới.

flashcards.back_en: To disagree and complain very strongly.
flashcards.example_en: People protested when the school was closed.
flashcards.example_vi: Mọi người phản đối khi ngôi trường bị đóng cửa.

flashcards.back_en: To organise activities to achieve something.
flashcards.example_en: She campaigns for girls' education.
flashcards.example_vi: Cô ấy vận động cho quyền học tập của trẻ em gái.

flashcards.back_en: So surprising that you can hardly believe it.
flashcards.example_en: I looked at it in amazement.
flashcards.example_vi: Em nhìn nó mà kinh ngạc.

flashcards.back_en: Making you feel happy and full of energy.
flashcards.example_en: I remember that feeling of excitement very well.
flashcards.example_vi: Em nhớ rất rõ cảm giác phấn khích đó.

flashcards.back_en: Making you feel very frightened.
flashcards.example_en: It was exciting and terrifying at the same time.
flashcards.example_vi: Nó vừa phấn khích vừa đáng sợ cùng một lúc.

flashcards.back_en: Pleased about something good you have done.
flashcards.example_en: I felt a sense of pride for doing something brave.
flashcards.example_vi: Em thấy tự hào vì đã làm được một việc dũng cảm.

flashcards.back_en: Pleased because you got what you wanted.
flashcards.example_en: I felt very satisfied because I had achieved something big.
flashcards.example_vi: Em thấy rất mãn nguyện vì đã làm được một việc lớn.

flashcards.back_en: Shaped like a bird's beak.
flashcards.example_en: My nose would be on the beaky side.
flashcards.example_vi: Mũi em thì hơi khoằm như mỏ chim.

flashcards.back_en: To move quickly with a short, light movement.
flashcards.example_en: I have white-blond hair that flicks around my face.
flashcards.example_vi: Em có mái tóc vàng bạch kim hất tung quanh mặt.

flashcards.back_en: Not like most others; not common.
flashcards.example_en: A girl with an unusual name tells her own story.
flashcards.example_vi: Một cô bé có cái tên khác thường tự kể chuyện mình.

flashcards.back_en: No. -tion is /ʃən/ 'shun'; -sion after a vowel is /ʒən/ 'zhun', as in decision.

flashcards.front_en: How do you ask about the equipment for a sport?
flashcards.back_en: 'What equipment do you need for …?' — 'You need a shuttlecock to play badminton.'

flashcards.front_en: What is the pattern of the 1st conditional?
flashcards.back_en: if / unless + present simple, then will or won't + verb. If you drink plenty of water, you'll stay hydrated.

flashcards.front_en: What does 'unless' mean in a 1st conditional?
flashcards.back_en: It means 'if … not'. Unless you eat enough carbohydrates = if you don't eat enough carbohydrates.

flashcards.front_en: Why avoid sugary food before sport?
flashcards.back_en: It gives a quick energy lift, but later you feel tired more quickly. Healthy carbohydrates last longer.

flashcards.front_en: need, should or mustn't — which is which?
flashcards.back_en: need = it is necessary; should = advice; mustn't = strong advice against doing something.

flashcards.front_en: Why warm up before you run?
flashcards.back_en: A warm-up gets your heart pumping and loosens your muscles; running on cold leg muscles can hurt them.

flashcards.front_en: Which two tenses does a sports biography use?
flashcards.back_en: Past simple for finished events with a date, present perfect for achievements that count up to now.

flashcards.front_en: Why put a quote in a biography?
flashcards.back_en: A quote gives the reader an idea of the person's personality. It can come from the person or from someone who knows them.

flashcards.front_en: How do you read a commentary with expression?
flashcards.back_en: Emphasise the key words — say them louder, longer and a little higher — and hurry over the small words.

flashcards.front_en: When do you use the present simple?
flashcards.back_en: For things that are always true, such as animal life cycles: emperor penguins live in the Antarctic.

flashcards.front_en: Two things penguin families do to survive the cold?
flashcards.back_en: The babies gather together for protection, and the chicks stay balanced on their mother's feet.

flashcards.front_en: What does every food chain start with?
flashcards.back_en: A plant, called the producer, because it makes its own food from the energy of the sun.

flashcards.front_en: who, which or whose — which one shows belonging?
flashcards.back_en: Whose: carnivores whose main diet is meat. Who is for people and animals, which for things.

flashcards.front_en: How do you build a wh- question?
flashcards.back_en: Question word + do or does + subject + base verb: 'Where do carnivorous plants grow?'

flashcards.front_en: What happens to your voice at the end of a wh- question?
flashcards.back_en: It falls on the last important word. A yes / no question rises at the end instead.

flashcards.front_en: How does the Sundew catch and eat an insect?
flashcards.back_en: Sticky liquid on its hairy leaves traps the insect, the leaf curls and crushes it, then juices dissolve it.

flashcards.front_en: Three rules for writing an infographic text?
flashcards.back_en: Use the present simple, keep the sentences short, and add a defining relative clause to say which animals you mean.

flashcards.front_en: Why does the author call Blue 55 'he' and not 'it'?
flashcards.back_en: It makes the whale feel like a person with feelings, so the reader has empathy for him.

flashcards.front_en: How do you say which gadget matters most to you?
flashcards.back_en: 'It's got to be my… because I can use it to…' Then compare: 'I think it's more useful than a…'

flashcards.front_en: When do you use the past simple?
flashcards.back_en: For finished actions in the past, usually with a time reference such as 'in 2014' or 'in the 1980s'.
Say when it happened and you need the past simple. Leave the time out and you need the present perfect.

flashcards.front_en: What comes after will and won't?
flashcards.back_en: The plain verb, with no 'to'. The form never changes: I will go, she will go, they will go.

flashcards.front_en: How do you ask a question with will?
flashcards.back_en: Put will in front of the subject: 'Will the boots save people money?' 'Which idea will the judges choose?'

flashcards.front_en: How do you start a sentence that gives your opinion?
flashcards.back_en: 'In my opinion, …' Then add reasons with 'This is because…' and examples with 'such as' or 'for example'.

flashcards.front_en: Why does a persuasive essay need reasons?
flashcards.back_en: Reasons are what persuade the reader to agree with you, so put your strongest reason first.
A verb of two parts, verb + preposition or adverb, like 'try out' or 'run off'. Together they mean something new.

flashcards.front_en: The two sounds of the letter 'a'
flashcards.back_en: Long /eɪ/ in lady, able and place; short /æ/ in strap, bag and have.

flashcards.front_en: How do you make a comparative adverb?
flashcards.back_en: Short adverbs add -er: longer, faster. Adverbs ending in -ly take 'more': more easily, more often, more carefully.

flashcards.front_en: What is the comparative of the adverb 'well'?
flashcards.back_en: 'Better', never 'more well'. The expensive brands are made better than the cheap ones.

flashcards.front_en: How do you work out the profit?
flashcards.back_en: Take all your costs away from the money you get from sales: $95.00 minus $15.00 leaves $80.00 profit.
'Several' is a smaller amount, about three or four. 'Plenty of' means lots.

flashcards.front_en: What do either… or and both of have in common?
flashcards.back_en: They always refer to two things: 'either Polar Bear Rescue or Global Welfare', 'both of these charities'.

flashcards.front_en: Two ways to make a suggestion in a discussion
flashcards.back_en: 'How about…?' and 'What about…?' Both are followed by verb + -ing: How about spending it on a class trip?

flashcards.front_en: How do you agree with only part of an idea?
flashcards.back_en: Say what you accept, then add 'but': 'We think it's a good idea to buy sports equipment, but not for the club.'

flashcards.front_en: When do you use a reflexive pronoun?
flashcards.back_en: To show that someone did it on their own, or when the subject and object are the same: 'I bought it myself.'

flashcards.front_en: What do connecting words do in an essay?
flashcards.back_en: They order your ideas: Firstly, Secondly and Finally for order, However for a contrast, because for a reason.
Two words used as one name. The first describes the second: website, science teacher, sports injury.

flashcards.front_en: Four adjective + preposition pairs to learn by heart?
flashcards.back_en: good at, keen on, interested in, fascinated by — and a noun comes after the preposition.

flashcards.front_en: Name three features that make a work uniform safe.
flashcards.back_en: A reflective stripe, a cap with a light on the front, and an alarm on the belt.

flashcards.front_en: How do you report what somebody said?
flashcards.back_en: say / tell + that + clause. Say goes straight to that; tell needs a person: She told me that…

flashcards.front_en: How do you make the opposites of fit, adventurous, enthusiastic?
flashcards.back_en: Add the prefix un-: unfit, unadventurous, unenthusiastic. But confident → shy and hardworking → lazy.

flashcards.front_en: Why do job adverts use the present continuous?
flashcards.back_en: Because the situation is temporary: We are looking for a friendly zookeeper.

flashcards.front_en: How do you shorten a sentence in an advert?
flashcards.back_en: Drop the pronoun, and be if you can: Must be able to do experiments. Experience needed.

flashcards.front_en: What does could + be mean in the poem?
flashcards.back_en: It is possible that you will be that thing. It is not permission and not a promise.

flashcards.front_en: Which three suffixes make the names of jobs?
flashcards.back_en: -er (builder), -or (actor), -ist (scientist).

flashcards.front_en: When do you use the past continuous?
flashcards.back_en: For a longer action already going on when a shorter one interrupted it. Form: was or were + verb-ing.

flashcards.front_en: Which tense goes with 'when the volcano suddenly exploded'?
flashcards.back_en: The past simple for the sudden event, the past continuous for the long one: We were making a film when it exploded.

flashcards.front_en: How does a storm cloud become electric?
flashcards.back_en: Storm winds make pieces of ice bump into each other, and that action creates an electric charge.

flashcards.front_en: Why does lightning strike trees and towers?
flashcards.back_en: Positive charge on the ground needs a tall object to connect with the negative charge at the bottom of the cloud.

flashcards.front_en: until, as soon as, while: what does each one mean?
flashcards.back_en: until = up to a point in time; as soon as = immediately after; while = at the same time as.

flashcards.front_en: How do you give short safety instructions?
flashcards.back_en: Use imperative verbs: Cover your head. Crawl under a strong table. Don't move from where you are.

flashcards.front_en: Which prepositions follow amazed, fascinated, interested and sad?
flashcards.back_en: amazed by, fascinated by, interested in, sad about.

flashcards.front_en: How should you begin a description of a place?
flashcards.back_en: With a surprising fact, to catch the reader's attention — for example an ash cloud over 20 kilometres high.

flashcards.front_en: What are matching sounds in a poem?
flashcards.back_en: Words placed close together that share a sound: the first consonant (warm, wonderful) or the vowel inside (bright, shining).
-ed says how a person feels; -ing describes the thing that causes the feeling.

flashcards.front_en: Name four features you can talk about in a film.
flashcards.back_en: The plot, the cast, the setting and the soundtrack. Also costumes, graphics and special effects.

flashcards.front_en: How do you make the past simple passive?
flashcards.back_en: was or were + past participle: These early films were made in black and white.

flashcards.front_en: When do you add 'by' to a passive sentence?
flashcards.back_en: When you want to name the doer: the first film projector was invented by the Edison company.

flashcards.front_en: Which time adverbs give an exact time?
flashcards.back_en: Today, tonight, daily and weekly. Often, usually and sometimes say how often, not when.

flashcards.front_en: Two ways to agree with your partner?
flashcards.back_en: I think that's a good idea. / Yes, that sounds right. / Me too.

flashcards.front_en: How do you punctuate direct speech?
flashcards.back_en: Speech marks around the spoken words, then a comma or an exclamation mark before the reporting verb.
Hard /θ/ in threw, thick, thought. Soft /ð/ in the, then. Same tongue, but soft th uses your voice.
Talking about people or things without saying exactly who, what or how many: someone, everybody, anywhere, nothing.
everyone is for people, everywhere is for places: There are art displays everywhere in my school.

flashcards.front_en: Present perfect for an unfinished past: when?
flashcards.back_en: For something that started in the past and is still true now: Ada has played in the Orchestra for many years.
Concrete nouns you can see, hear, touch, smell or taste (violin). Abstract nouns are ideas and feelings (pride).

flashcards.front_en: Which present tense for a fixed timetable?
flashcards.back_en: The present simple: Their train leaves early on Wednesday morning.

flashcards.front_en: Which present tense for a plan you have arranged?
flashcards.back_en: The present continuous: They are arriving on Sunday and staying until Wednesday.

flashcards.front_en: What are the two uses of 'like'?
flashcards.back_en: Verb: I like the shape of that building. Preposition: It looks like the sails on a ship.

flashcards.front_en: What order do adjectives go in before a noun?
flashcards.back_en: Number, opinion, size, physical quality, colour, material: a single broken crayon; a beautiful red sunset.

flashcards.front_en: When is the letter i /aɪ/ and when is it /ɪ/?
flashcards.back_en: /aɪ/ in silent, icy and smile; /ɪ/ in still, pink and gift, where consonants close the syllable.
The small light object that you hit over the net in badminton.
flashcards.example_en: You need a shuttlecock to play badminton.
flashcards.example_vi: Bạn cần một quả cầu để chơi cầu lông.

flashcards.back_en: A bat with strings, used in tennis and badminton.
flashcards.example_en: She holds the racquet in her right hand when she serves.
flashcards.example_vi: Bạn ấy cầm vợt bằng tay phải khi giao bóng.

flashcards.back_en: Special glasses that protect your eyes, for example when you swim.
flashcards.example_en: Swimmers wear goggles so that the water does not hurt their eyes.
flashcards.example_vi: Người bơi đeo kính bơi để nước không làm cay mắt.

flashcards.back_en: Hard pads that protect the front of your lower legs.
flashcards.example_en: Footballers wear shin pads to protect the front of their legs.
flashcards.example_vi: Cầu thủ bóng đá đeo bọc ống chân để bảo vệ phần trước cẳng chân.

flashcards.back_en: The two posts that stand at each end of a football or hockey pitch.
flashcards.example_en: The ball hit the goalposts and bounced back onto the pitch.
flashcards.example_vi: Quả bóng đập vào cột gôn rồi bật ngược lại sân.

flashcards.back_en: Material with holes in it, stretched across a court or across a goal.
flashcards.example_en: In tennis and volleyball you have to hit the ball over the net.
flashcards.example_vi: Trong quần vợt và bóng chuyền, bạn phải đánh bóng qua lưới.

flashcards.back_en: A long stick with a curved end, used to hit the ball in hockey.
flashcards.example_en: You need a hockey stick and a small hard ball to play hockey.
flashcards.example_vi: Bạn cần một cây gậy và một quả bóng nhỏ cứng để chơi khúc côn cầu.

flashcards.back_en: A band you wear around your waist; in judo its colour shows your level.
flashcards.example_en: In judo, the colour of your belt shows how much you have learned.
flashcards.example_vi: Trong judo, màu đai cho biết bạn đã học được tới đâu.

flashcards.back_en: A substance in food that provides the body with energy.
flashcards.example_en: Eat healthy carbohydrates like wholemeal bread, pasta and brown rice.
flashcards.example_vi: Hãy ăn tinh bột lành mạnh như bánh mì nguyên cám, mì ống và gạo lứt.

flashcards.back_en: Substances you need to live and grow.
flashcards.example_en: Your blood cells carry nutrients and oxygen to your muscles.
flashcards.example_vi: Các tế bào máu mang chất dinh dưỡng và ô-xy tới cơ bắp của bạn.

flashcards.back_en: A chemical you need to live and breathe.
flashcards.example_en: You breathe faster during exercise because your muscles need more oxygen.
flashcards.example_vi: Bạn thở gấp hơn khi tập luyện vì cơ bắp cần nhiều ô-xy hơn.

flashcards.back_en: To change food so your body can use it.
flashcards.example_en: A banana is easy to digest before you do sport.
flashcards.example_vi: Quả chuối rất dễ tiêu hoá trước khi bạn chơi thể thao.

flashcards.back_en: A substance in food that repairs your muscles and helps you get stronger.
flashcards.example_en: Chicken, fish, eggs and lentils are good protein foods.
flashcards.example_vi: Thịt gà, cá, trứng và đậu lăng là những món giàu chất đạm.

flashcards.back_en: A substance that gives you strong bones.
flashcards.example_en: Milk and yoghurt contain calcium to give you strong bones.
flashcards.example_vi: Sữa và sữa chua có canxi giúp xương chắc khoẻ.

flashcards.back_en: Having enough water in your body.
flashcards.example_en: If you drink plenty of water, you'll stay cool and hydrated.
flashcards.example_vi: Nếu bạn uống đủ nước, bạn sẽ mát mẻ và không bị thiếu nước.

flashcards.back_en: The joint between your foot and your leg.
flashcards.example_en: Rotate your ankle slowly ten times in each direction.
flashcards.example_vi: Hãy xoay cổ chân thật chậm mười vòng mỗi chiều.

flashcards.back_en: The joint where your arm joins your body.
flashcards.example_en: Turn your shoulders in big circles to warm up your upper body.
flashcards.example_vi: Xoay vai thành vòng lớn để khởi động phần thân trên.

flashcards.back_en: The top part of your leg, above the knee.
flashcards.example_en: Running uses the big muscles in your thighs.
flashcards.example_vi: Chạy bộ dùng đến những cơ lớn ở đùi.

flashcards.back_en: A muscle at the back of your thigh.
flashcards.example_en: Stretch your hamstrings before you sprint.
flashcards.example_vi: Hãy giãn cơ gân kheo trước khi chạy nước rút.

flashcards.back_en: The joint where your leg joins your body.
flashcards.example_en: You should warm up your hips too.
flashcards.example_vi: Bạn cũng nên khởi động phần hông.

flashcards.back_en: The joint in the middle of your leg.
flashcards.example_en: Bend your knees a little before you jump.
flashcards.example_vi: Hãy hơi khuỵu gối trước khi bật nhảy.

flashcards.back_en: The five parts at the end of your foot.
flashcards.example_en: Stand up straight and try to touch your toes.
flashcards.example_vi: Đứng thẳng người rồi cố chạm vào các ngón chân.

flashcards.back_en: The organ that pumps blood around your body.
flashcards.example_en: First, we need to get your heart pumping.
flashcards.example_vi: Trước tiên, chúng ta cần làm cho tim đập nhanh lên.

flashcards.back_en: A person who does gymnastics.
flashcards.example_en: Simone Biles is the most successful gymnast of all time.
flashcards.example_vi: Simone Biles là vận động viên thể dục dụng cụ thành công nhất mọi thời đại.

flashcards.back_en: A natural ability to do something well.
flashcards.example_en: A coach noticed her natural talent and invited her to join a class.
flashcards.example_vi: Một huấn luyện viên nhận ra tài năng thiên bẩm của cô bé và mời cô vào lớp.

flashcards.back_en: A person who trains a sports player or a team.
flashcards.example_en: Her coach helped her to train for the World Championships.
flashcards.example_vi: Huấn luyện viên đã giúp cô luyện tập cho Giải vô địch thế giới.

flashcards.back_en: When a family looks after a child who is not their own.
flashcards.example_en: She was in foster care until her grandparents adopted her.
flashcards.example_vi: Cô sống ở gia đình chăm sóc tạm thời cho tới khi được ông bà nhận nuôi.

flashcards.back_en: To laugh at someone in an unkind way.
flashcards.example_en: In third grade, she was teased about her muscly legs.
flashcards.example_vi: Hồi lớp ba, cô từng bị trêu chọc vì đôi chân nhiều cơ bắp.

flashcards.back_en: To get better at something.
flashcards.example_en: She used the experience to improve.
flashcards.example_vi: Cô đã dùng trải nghiệm đó để tiến bộ hơn.

flashcards.back_en: A problem that stops your progress for a while.
flashcards.example_en: Missing the National team in 2011 was a big setback.
flashcards.example_vi: Việc lỡ suất vào đội tuyển quốc gia năm 2011 là một trắc trở lớn.

flashcards.back_en: To stop trying.
flashcards.example_en: Simone has had setbacks, but she has never given up.
flashcards.example_vi: Simone từng gặp trắc trở, nhưng cô chưa bao giờ bỏ cuộc.

flashcards.back_en: A person who describes a game while it is happening.
flashcards.example_en: Danny acted as commentator so that his dad could follow the game.
flashcards.example_vi: Danny làm bình luận viên để bố có thể theo dõi trận đấu.

flashcards.back_en: A player whose job is to score goals.
flashcards.example_en: The United defenders struggled to keep up with City's strikers.
flashcards.example_vi: Các hậu vệ United chật vật theo kịp những tiền đạo của City.

flashcards.back_en: A player whose job is to stop the other team scoring.
flashcards.example_en: The ball ricocheted off a defender to Owusu.
flashcards.example_vi: Quả bóng bật ra từ chân một hậu vệ tới chỗ Owusu.

flashcards.back_en: The player who stands in the goal and stops shots.
flashcards.example_en: He fired an unstoppable volley past the United keeper.
flashcards.example_vi: Anh ấy tung cú vô-lê không thể cản phá qua thủ môn của United.

flashcards.back_en: The middle part of a football pitch, between the two goals.
flashcards.example_en: City's midfield dynamo launched a high cross into the United area.
flashcards.example_vi: Nhạc trưởng tuyến giữa của City tạt một quả bổng vào vòng cấm United.

flashcards.back_en: To kick or hit a ball before it touches the ground.
flashcards.example_en: Owusu controlled the ball on his knee and volleyed it with amazing power.
flashcards.example_vi: Owusu đỡ bóng bằng đầu gối rồi vô-lê với lực cực mạnh.

flashcards.back_en: To kick or hit something very hard and fast.
flashcards.example_en: He just blasted it in!
flashcards.example_vi: Cậu ấy nã thẳng bóng vào lưới!

flashcards.back_en: To jump high or a long way.
flashcards.example_en: Danny and his dad leapt into each other's arms as the crowd exploded.
flashcards.example_vi: Danny và bố nhảy cẫng lên ôm chầm lấy nhau khi khán đài vỡ oà.

flashcards.back_en: A baby bird.
flashcards.example_en: The chicks stay balanced on their mother's feet.
flashcards.example_vi: Những chú chim non đứng thăng bằng trên chân mẹ.

flashcards.back_en: When an egg breaks and a young bird comes out.
flashcards.example_en: Daylight appears again and thousands of chicks hatch.
flashcards.example_vi: Ánh sáng ban ngày quay trở lại và hàng nghìn chim non nở ra.

flashcards.back_en: To produce young animals.
flashcards.example_en: Emperor penguins breed in the coldest place on Earth.
flashcards.example_vi: Chim cánh cụt hoàng đế sinh sản ở nơi lạnh nhất Trái Đất.

flashcards.back_en: An animal's partner, for producing young.
flashcards.example_en: Each penguin finds a mate before the long winter begins.
flashcards.example_vi: Mỗi con chim cánh cụt tìm một bạn đời trước khi mùa đông dài bắt đầu.

flashcards.back_en: To stand very close together to keep warm.
flashcards.example_en: The penguins huddle together when the freezing wind blows.
flashcards.example_vi: Đàn chim cánh cụt xúm sát vào nhau khi gió lạnh buốt thổi tới.

flashcards.back_en: A group of birds that live together.
flashcards.example_en: Emperor penguins live in a huge colony on the ice.
flashcards.example_vi: Chim cánh cụt hoàng đế sống thành một quần thể khổng lồ trên mặt băng.

flashcards.back_en: To stay alive in difficult conditions.
flashcards.example_en: Penguin families survive the extreme cold of Antarctica.
flashcards.example_vi: Các gia đình chim cánh cụt sống sót qua cái lạnh khắc nghiệt ở Nam Cực.

flashcards.back_en: A living thing that makes its own food; every food chain starts with one.
flashcards.example_en: The plant is called a producer because it makes its own food from the sun.
flashcards.example_vi: Cây được gọi là sinh vật sản xuất vì nó tự tạo ra thức ăn từ ánh nắng.

flashcards.back_en: A living thing that gets its food by eating other living things.
flashcards.example_en: The next link in the food chain is called a consumer.
flashcards.example_vi: Mắt xích tiếp theo trong chuỗi thức ăn được gọi là sinh vật tiêu thụ.

flashcards.back_en: An animal that only eats plants.
flashcards.example_en: Rabbits, mice and grasshoppers are herbivores.
flashcards.example_vi: Thỏ, chuột và châu chấu là những loài ăn cỏ.

flashcards.back_en: An animal whose main diet is meat.
flashcards.example_en: Frogs, lizards and spiders are small carnivores.
flashcards.example_vi: Ếch, thằn lằn và nhện là những loài ăn thịt cỡ nhỏ.

flashcards.back_en: An animal that eats both plants and meat.
flashcards.example_en: An omnivore can be a secondary or a tertiary consumer.
flashcards.example_vi: Loài ăn tạp có thể là sinh vật tiêu thụ bậc hai hoặc bậc ba.

flashcards.back_en: An animal that hunts and eats other animals.
flashcards.example_en: Top predators like lions and sharks have no natural enemies.
flashcards.example_vi: Những kẻ săn mồi đầu bảng như sư tử và cá mập không có kẻ thù tự nhiên.

flashcards.back_en: The way living things affect each other and the environment.
flashcards.example_en: All animals and plants are important in our planet's ecosystem.
flashcards.example_vi: Mọi loài động vật và thực vật đều quan trọng trong hệ sinh thái của hành tinh.

flashcards.back_en: The food and drink that a living thing needs.
flashcards.example_en: These creatures are carnivores whose main diet is meat.
flashcards.example_vi: Những sinh vật này là loài ăn thịt, thức ăn chính của chúng là thịt.

flashcards.back_en: The natural place where an animal or a plant lives.
flashcards.example_en: The polar bear's habitat is the ice around the North Pole.
flashcards.example_vi: Môi trường sống của gấu Bắc Cực là vùng băng quanh Bắc Cực.

flashcards.back_en: Meat-eating; a carnivorous plant eats insects and other small animals.
flashcards.example_en: Where do carnivorous plants grow?
flashcards.example_vi: Cây ăn thịt mọc ở đâu?

flashcards.back_en: An animal that another living thing catches and eats.
flashcards.example_en: How does a carnivorous plant catch its prey?
flashcards.example_vi: Cây ăn thịt bắt con mồi bằng cách nào?

flashcards.back_en: A very thin thread that grows on skin, or on the leaf of a plant.
flashcards.example_en: The Sundew plant has long thin leaves covered in tiny hairs.
flashcards.example_vi: Cây gọng vó có những chiếc lá dài mảnh phủ đầy lông tơ.

flashcards.back_en: Holding on to whatever it touches.
flashcards.example_en: The insect is held by the thick sticky liquid on the leaf.
flashcards.example_vi: Con côn trùng bị giữ lại bởi lớp chất lỏng dính đặc trên lá.

flashcards.back_en: Something that flows, like water.
flashcards.example_en: The leaves are covered in a thick sticky liquid.
flashcards.example_vi: Những chiếc lá phủ đầy một lớp chất lỏng dính đặc.

flashcards.back_en: To catch something so that it cannot escape.
flashcards.example_en: When an insect crawls onto the leaves, it is trapped.
flashcards.example_vi: Khi một con côn trùng bò lên lá, nó bị mắc bẫy.

flashcards.back_en: To press something so hard that it breaks.
flashcards.example_en: Then the leaf curls around the insect and crushes it.
flashcards.example_vi: Sau đó chiếc lá cuộn lại quanh con côn trùng và nghiền nát nó.

flashcards.back_en: To make something break down in a liquid.
flashcards.example_en: The juices of the plant slowly dissolve the insect.
flashcards.example_vi: Dịch của cây từ từ làm tan rã con côn trùng.

flashcards.back_en: An animal which can live in water and on land.
flashcards.example_en: Frogs, toads, salamanders and newts are amphibians.
flashcards.example_vi: Ếch, cóc, kỳ giông và sa giông là động vật lưỡng cư.

flashcards.back_en: An animal that has a spine, or back bone.
flashcards.example_en: Amphibians are vertebrates, which means they have a back bone.
flashcards.example_vi: Động vật lưỡng cư là động vật có xương sống, nghĩa là chúng có cột sống.

flashcards.back_en: A little bit wet.
flashcards.example_en: Amphibians need a moist environment to survive.
flashcards.example_vi: Động vật lưỡng cư cần môi trường ẩm ướt để sống.

flashcards.back_en: The parts a fish or a young amphibian uses to breathe under water.
flashcards.example_en: Most amphibians have lungs and gills.
flashcards.example_vi: Phần lớn động vật lưỡng cư có cả phổi lẫn mang.

flashcards.back_en: The two organs in the chest that an animal breathes with.
flashcards.example_en: When they develop legs and lungs, they move onto the land.
flashcards.example_vi: Khi mọc chân và có phổi, chúng chuyển lên cạn để sống.

flashcards.back_en: Small hard plates that cover the skin of a fish or a reptile.
flashcards.example_en: The chameleon has scales but the whale has smooth skin.
flashcards.example_vi: Tắc kè hoa có vảy còn cá voi thì da trơn nhẵn.

flashcards.back_en: The flat parts a fish uses to swim.
flashcards.example_en: A fish uses its fins to push itself through the water.
flashcards.example_vi: Cá dùng vây để đẩy mình đi trong nước.

flashcards.back_en: The light soft parts that cover a bird's body.
flashcards.example_en: Birds are the only animals with feathers.
flashcards.example_vi: Chim là loài động vật duy nhất có lông vũ.

flashcards.back_en: A very large area of sea.
flashcards.example_en: The video started out with a whale swimming in the ocean.
flashcards.example_vi: Đoạn phim mở đầu bằng cảnh một con cá voi bơi giữa đại dương.

flashcards.back_en: A group of whales.
flashcards.example_en: Blue 55 swam around by himself and not in a pod.
flashcards.example_vi: Blue 55 bơi một mình chứ không đi theo đàn.

flashcards.back_en: Very small plants and animals that bigger sea animals eat.
flashcards.example_en: Baleen whales eat plankton and small fish.
flashcards.example_vi: Cá voi tấm sừng ăn sinh vật phù du và cá nhỏ.

flashcards.back_en: A group of animals that are very similar.
flashcards.example_en: The skin sample showed that his parents had been different species.
flashcards.example_vi: Mẫu da cho thấy bố mẹ của nó thuộc hai loài khác nhau.

flashcards.back_en: A mixture of two very different things.
flashcards.example_en: Blue 55 is a hybrid: his mother was a blue whale and his father a fin whale.
flashcards.example_vi: Blue 55 là một con lai: mẹ nó là cá voi xanh còn bố là cá voi vây.

flashcards.back_en: A scientist who studies sea life.
flashcards.example_en: Marine biologists figured out why the whale was all alone in the ocean.
flashcards.example_vi: Các nhà sinh vật biển đã tìm ra vì sao con cá voi lại lẻ loi giữa đại dương.

flashcards.back_en: When animals travel to a different place.
flashcards.example_en: The researchers wanted to follow his migration pattern.
flashcards.example_vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu muốn theo dõi lộ trình di cư của nó.

flashcards.back_en: A safe place for animals.
flashcards.example_en: Researchers from a marine sanctuary tried to put a tracker on him.
flashcards.example_vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu từ một khu bảo tồn biển đã thử gắn thiết bị theo dõi lên nó.

flashcards.back_en: A small useful tool or machine.
flashcards.example_en: What is your favourite gadget or piece of equipment?
flashcards.example_vi: Món đồ công nghệ hay dụng cụ nào em thích nhất?

flashcards.back_en: The things you need in order to do an activity.
flashcards.example_en: My mountain bike is the most important piece of equipment for me.
flashcards.example_vi: Chiếc xe đạp địa hình là dụng cụ quan trọng nhất với em.

flashcards.back_en: A small flat computer with a touch screen.
flashcards.example_en: It's got to be my tablet – I can't live without it!
