quiz.stem_en: Sound first appeared in films in 1927. What were these new films with sound called?
quiz.why_en: Films with sound and dialogue were called talkies (p.130).

quiz.stem_en: Audiences could buy popcorn in cinemas from 1912. Which sentence says this in the past simple passive?

choices.en: Popcorn was sold in cinemas from 1912.
Popcorn were sold in cinemas from 1912.
Popcorn is selling in cinemas from 1912.

quiz.why_en: Popcorn is singular and the event is past, so it takes was + sold (p.130).

quiz.stem_en: Which adverb does NOT give an exact time?
quiz.why_en: Today, daily and weekly are definite; often only says how much, not when (p.133).

quiz.stem_en: Complete this warning: 'Too much screen time can make you ___ to your device.'
quiz.why_en: Being addicted means you cannot stop using it (p.132).

quiz.stem_en: Your partner says, 'I think we should have no devices at family meals.' Which reply agrees with them?

choices.en: Actually, I think it's better to keep them with us.
I'm not really sure that would work for us.
I don't agree with that idea at all.
I think that's a good idea, and me too.

quiz.why_en: 'I think that's a good idea' and 'Me too' are the phrases for agreeing (p.133).

quiz.stem_en: Which line of direct speech is punctuated correctly?

choices.en: Oh, no, not again! sighed Dad.

quiz.why_en: The spoken words sit inside speech marks and keep their exclamation mark before the reporting verb (p.135).

quiz.stem_en: Boris was hiding a nasty trick, so he laughed quietly and unkindly. Complete: 'Here, let me make it more comfortable for you,' he ___.
quiz.why_en: To snigger is to laugh quietly in an unkind way (p.135).

quiz.stem_en: In 'the lizard stood on its hind legs', what does hind mean?
quiz.why_en: Hind legs are the legs at the back of an animal (p.139).

quiz.stem_en: In which word does th have the soft, voiced sound /ð/?
quiz.why_en: Then is /ðen/ with the voice on; threw, thick and thought all use the hard /θ/ (p.139).

quiz.stem_en: Jurassic Park was made in 1993. Why is it important in cinema history?

choices.en: It used CGI to bring life-like dinosaurs to the screen.
It was the first film ever shown with sound in a cinema.
It was the first film that was made in colour.
It was the first film to be based on a novel.

quiz.why_en: Its Computer Generated Imagery was so good that many later films copied the technology (p.136).

quiz.stem_en: Complete: 'Art in public spaces is a good idea because ___ can enjoy it.'
quiz.why_en: The pronoun stands for people, so it must end in -one (p.145).

quiz.stem_en: Complete: 'There isn't ___ in my town where you can see street art.'
quiz.why_en: After a negative verb such as isn't, English uses any-, and the word stands for a place (p.145).

quiz.stem_en: Which word means a large picture painted on a wall?
quiz.why_en: A mural is painted straight onto a wall (p.145).

quiz.stem_en: Which word means a picture made from many small coloured pieces stuck together?
quiz.why_en: A mosaic is built up from small coloured pieces (p.145).

quiz.stem_en: Complete: 'Ada ___ in the Orchestra for many years, and she still plays with them today.'
quiz.why_en: The time started in the past and has not finished, so use the present perfect (p.147).

quiz.stem_en: Complete: 'The instruments ___ hundreds of children the gift of music, and they are still doing it.'
quiz.why_en: Have or has plus the past participle covers a time that reaches up to now (p.147).

quiz.stem_en: Which is a percussion instrument, one that you play by hitting it?
quiz.why_en: You hit a drum, while a violin has strings and the other two are played by blowing (p.146).

quiz.stem_en: In Cateura, Paraguay, the young musicians play instruments built out of rubbish. Why?

choices.en: Their families cannot afford to buy real instruments.
They like the sound of tins better than the sound of wood.
There is no music school in the town for them to join.
They want to win a prize for the strangest instruments.

quiz.why_en: The music school had too few instruments and the children could not afford to play otherwise (p.146).

quiz.stem_en: Complete this sentence about a fixed timetable: 'Their train ___ early on Wednesday morning.'
quiz.why_en: A timetable is a fact, so the future event takes the present simple (p.149).

quiz.stem_en: The family have already booked their trip. Complete: 'They ___ on Sunday and staying until Wednesday.'
quiz.why_en: The present continuous shows a plan that has already been arranged (p.149).

quiz.stem_en: One event asks you to download a city map and find animal artworks all over the city centre. What kind of activity is it?

choices.en: a workshop where you make your own sculpture
a quiz you complete to win two free tickets
a circus show with acrobatics and music
a treasure hunt that takes you round the city

quiz.why_en: The Art Safari is a treasure hunt: you follow a map to find the artworks (p.148).

quiz.stem_en: In which sentence is 'like' a preposition that compares two things?

choices.en: It looks like the sails on a ship.
I like the shape of that building.
Which building do you like best?
My friends like drawing tall buildings.

quiz.why_en: After look, sound or feel, 'like' plus a noun compares two things (p.151).

quiz.stem_en: Which adjective means the deep blue colour of a precious stone?
quiz.why_en: Sapphire glass is the deep blue of the stone of the same name (p.151).

quiz.stem_en: Complete this line from a poem about a building: 'I am made of smooth concrete and ___ glass.'
quiz.why_en: Gleaming means clean, bright and shiny, which is how glass looks (p.150).

quiz.stem_en: Which phrase has its adjectives in the correct order?
quiz.why_en: Number comes before physical quality; the others put colour, physical quality or size in the wrong place (p.155).

quiz.stem_en: In which word is the letter i pronounced /aɪ/?
quiz.why_en: The silent e makes smile /smaɪl/, while the other three have the short /ɪ/ (p.154).

quiz.stem_en: Willow paints a pink tree and her teacher asks who ever heard of one. What does Willow answer?

choices.en: I ran out of green paint this morning.
That's what I saw when I closed my eyes.
My art book says trees are always pink.
I wanted to make my classmates laugh.

quiz.why_en: Willow repeats this line in the story, and it shows where her ideas come from (p.152).

quiz.stem_en: Complete: 'Miss Hawthorn's icy blue eyes ___ at Willow.' Choose the verb that means looked angrily.
quiz.why_en: To glare is to look at someone in an angry way (p.154).
